explicacao: Nero se apresentava em público como ator, poeta, músico e condutor de carros de corrida, o que escandalizava a aristocracia romana, porque esses ofícios costumavam ser de escravos e artistas de má fama. Plínio o chamou de "imperador-ator". Para a Olimpíada de 67, além de conseguir o adiamento, ele fez incluir competições artísticas entre as provas atléticas. Durante os Jogos, hospedado numa vila construída para ele em Olímpia, cantou e tocou lira no palco, atuou em tragédias e disputou corridas de carros. Venceu todas as provas de que participou. Na corrida de dez cavalos, foi lançado para fora do carro e abandonou a prova, mas recebeu a coroa assim mesmo, sob o argumento de que teria vencido se tivesse terminado. Segundo o historiador Edward Champlin, a presença do imperador sufocou qualquer competição de verdade, e Nero parecia não perceber isso. A glória durou pouco: ele morreu um ano depois, e seu nome foi apagado da lista de vencedores.

fontes.trecho: He made public appearances as an actor, poet, musician, and charioteer, which scandalized his aristocratic contemporaries as these occupations were usually the domain of slaves, public entertainers, and infamous persons. [...] He stayed at the Villa of Nero at Olympia, Greece, during his participation at the Olympic Games of AD 67. [...] Pliny described Nero as an "actor-emperor" (scaenici imperatoris) [...] In AD 67 Nero participated in the Olympics. He had bribed organizers to postpone the games for a year so he could participate, and artistic competitions were added to the athletic events. Nero won every contest in which he was a competitor. During the games Nero sang and played his lyre on stage, acted in tragedies and raced chariots. He won a 10-horse chariot race, despite being thrown from the chariot and leaving the race. He was crowned on the basis that he would have won if he had completed the race. After he died a year later, his name was removed from the list of winners. Champlin writes that though Nero's participation "effectively stifled true competition, [Nero] seems to have been oblivious of reality."

gancho: O revezamento da tocha olímpica parece tradição grega, mas não existia nos Jogos antigos: foi criado para os Jogos de Berlim de 1936, sob o nazismo, com tochas da Krupp e espelho da Zeiss.
explicacao: Na Grécia antiga havia, sim, fogo sagrado em Olímpia: durante os Jogos, uma chama ficava acesa no altar do santuário de Héstia, e outros fogos eram acesos nos templos de Zeus e de Hera. Mas ninguém levava esse fogo de cidade em cidade. Nos Jogos modernos, a primeira chama simbólica apareceu em Amsterdã, em 1928, numa ideia do arquiteto Jan Wils: ela ardia no alto de uma torre do estádio para indicar de longe onde aconteciam as provas, e foi acesa por um funcionário da companhia elétrica da cidade. O revezamento veio oito anos depois, criado por Carl Diem para Berlim. A primeira cerimônia de acendimento em Olímpia foi em 20 de julho de 1936, com tochas fabricadas pela Krupp e um espelho da Zeiss, duas empresas ligadas ao governo nazista. A chama percorreu 3.187 km, carregada por 3.331 corredores durante doze dias e onze noites, e o ministro da Propaganda, Joseph Goebbels, encomendou a Leni Riefenstahl um filme sobre o trajeto. Até hoje a chama é acesa diante das ruínas do templo de Hera, com os raios do Sol concentrados por um espelho parabólico.

fontes.trecho: The first time that a symbolic flame made its appearance in the Summer Olympic Games was for the 1928 Summer Olympics in Amsterdam. The main purpose of this fire, placed in a large bowl on top of a slender tower, named "Marathon Tower", was to indicate for miles around where in Amsterdam the Olympic Games were being held. This tower was associated with the marathon race and all its elements, including the fire, were an idea of the architect Jan Wils who also had designed the stadium. The idea for the Olympic flame was derived from ancient Greek ceremonies where a sacred fire was kept burning throughout the celebration of the ancient Olympics on the altar of the sanctuary of Hestia. [...] Every four years, when Zeus was honoured at the Olympic Games, additional fires were lit at his temple and that of his wife, Hera. The modern Olympic flame is ignited every two years in front of the ruins of the temple of Hera. When the idea of a symbolic fire was introduced during the 1928 Summer Olympics, an employee of the Electric Utility of Amsterdam lit the first symbolic flame in the Marathon Tower of the Olympic Stadium in Amsterdam. The Olympic flame and the Olympic torch relay was first introduced to the Summer Olympics at the 1936 Summer Olympics in Berlin by Carl Diem. The first ever torch-lighting ceremony was held in Olympia, Greece on July 20, 1936. The torches used were made by Krupp, and the mirror used to light the flame was made by Zeiss Optics, both companies with links to the Nazi government of the time. [...] a fire is kindled by the light of the Sun, its rays concentrated by a parabolic mirror. [...] The Olympic torch relay, which transports the Olympic flame from Olympia, Greece to the various designated sites of the Games, had no ancient precedent and was introduced by Carl Diem at the 1936 Summer Olympics in Berlin, Germany. At the first Olympic torch relay, the flame was transported from Olympia to Berlin over 3,187 kilometers (1,980 miles) by 3,331 runners in twelve days and eleven nights. Nazi Propaganda Minister Joseph Goebbels commissioned filmmaker and propagandist Leni Riefenstahl to film the event.

gancho: A Olimpíada de 1956 foi em Melbourne, mas o hipismo foi na Suécia, meses antes do resto: a quarentena australiana para cavalos era tão rígida que o país não abriu exceção nem para os Jogos.
explicacao: A Austrália exigia que cavalos importados cumprissem seis meses de quarentena antes do embarque. Numa reunião em 1953, as autoridades federais decidiram não mudar a lei por causa dos animais olímpicos, e as provas equestres ficaram impossíveis no país. Em 1954, o Comitê Olímpico Internacional escolheu Estocolmo como sede alternativa. O resultado foi uma Olimpíada dividida entre duas cidades, dois países e dois continentes: o hipismo, com adestramento, concurso completo e saltos, foi de 11 a 17 de junho, no verão do hemisfério norte, e as demais modalidades, em novembro, no fim da primavera australiana. Foram 158 inscrições de 29 comitês olímpicos. Até a tocha teve trajeto próprio: todos os que a levaram até Estocolmo foram a cavalo. A separação teve um efeito curioso: cinco países competiram na Suécia e não foram a Melbourne. Egito e Camboja ficaram de fora por causa da Crise de Suez, e Holanda, Espanha e Suíça boicotaram a parte australiana em protesto contra a invasão soviética da Hungria.

fontes.trecho: The equestrian events at the 1956 Summer Olympics were held in Stockholm due to the Australian quarantine regulations and included dressage, eventing, and show jumping. [...] The competitions were held from 11 to 17 June 1956 at Stockholm Olympic Stadium. There were 158 entries from 29 National Olympic Committees [...] Although Melbourne was awarded the 1956 Olympic Games, Australia had a strict six-month pre-shipment quarantine on horses. A meeting in 1953 by Australian federal authorities ruled that they would not change the quarantine laws for the Olympic horses. Therefore, the equestrian competition would not be able to be held in Australia. In 1954, the IOC selected Stockholm, Sweden, as the alternate venue for the equestrian events. Therefore, the equestrian events were not only separated by city or country, but also continent, with the equestrian event being held in June (summer in the Northern Hemisphere) and the other sports held in November (late spring in the Southern Hemisphere). [...] Five nations competed in the equestrian events in Stockholm, but did not attend the Games in Melbourne: [...] Egypt and Cambodia did not compete in Melbourne due to the Suez Crisis, whilst Netherlands, Spain and Switzerland all boycotted the Australian event in protest at the Soviet invasion of Hungary.
In 1956, all carriers in the torch relay to Stockholm, where the equestrian events were held instead of in Melbourne, travelled on horseback.

gancho: O campeão da maratona olímpica de 1936 era coreano, mas correu pelo Japão, que dominava a Coreia. Um jornal apagou a bandeira japonesa da camisa dele na foto do pódio, e oito pessoas acabaram presas.
explicacao: Sohn Kee-chung nasceu em 1912 na Coreia, então sob domínio japonês, e por ordem de Tóquio competiu com o nome Son Kitei, a pronúncia japonesa dos caracteres do seu nome. Em Berlim, venceu a maratona em 2h29min19s, recorde olímpico, e o companheiro Nam Sung-yong levou o bronze; as duas medalhas foram creditadas ao Japão. Na cerimônia, Sohn se recusou a reconhecer o hino japonês e depois disse a jornalistas que tinha vergonha de correr pelo Japão. Quando o jornal Dong-a Ilbo publicou a foto do pódio, retocou a imagem para sumir com a bandeira japonesa da camisa. O governador-geral japonês da Coreia ficou furioso: a polícia militar prendeu oito pessoas ligadas ao jornal, que foi suspenso por nove meses. Sohn também deveria ter ganhado um capacete coríntio da Grécia antiga, achado em Olímpia, mas o COI achou que um presente tão valioso violaria as regras do amadorismo. O capacete ficou 50 anos num museu de Berlim e só lhe foi entregue em 1986. Em 2011, o COI passou a registrar a nacionalidade coreana no perfil oficial dele.

fontes.trecho: He became the first  Korean to win a medal at the Olympic Games, winning gold in the marathon at the 1936 Berlin Olympics. He was born in the Korean Peninsula, but he was forced to compete as a member of the Japanese delegation because Korea was under Japanese rule at the time. Sohn set an Olympic record of 2 hours 29 minutes 19.2 seconds. [...] Sohn Kee-chung was born on August 29, 1912 [...] His teammate Nam Sung-yong took the bronze medal. As Korea was under Japanese rule at the time, the International Olympic Committee (IOC) officially credited Japan with Sohn's gold and Nam's bronze in the 1936 Summer Olympics medal count. On December 9, 2011, the IOC recognized Sohn's Korean nationality in his official profile. [...] Under orders from Tokyo, Sohn Kee-chung had to compete using the Latin alphabet name of Son Kitei. It is the romanization of the Japanese pronunciation of his Korean name in hanja. Sohn refused to acknowledge the Japanese anthem while it was played at his award ceremony and later told reporters that he was ashamed to run for Japan. When the Dong-a Ilbo published a photograph of Sohn at the medal ceremony, it altered the image to remove the Japanese flag from his running tunic. The act enraged the Japanese Governor-General of Korea Minami Jiro in Seoul. The Kempetai military police imprisoned eight people connected with the newspaper and suspended its publication for nine months. [...] For winning the marathon, Sohn was to have received an ancient Corinthian helmet from the 8th century BC, which was discovered at Olympia, Greece, and later purchased by a newspaper in Athens to give as an Olympic award. However, the IOC believed that presenting such a valuable gift to a runner would violate its amateur rules. The helmet was placed in a Berlin museum and remained there for 50 years. It was finally presented to Sohn in 1986.

gancho: Em 1936, dois amigos japoneses empataram no salto com vara e se recusaram a desempatar. A equipe deu prata a um e bronze ao outro; no Japão, eles cortaram as medalhas ao meio e juntaram as metades.
explicacao: Shuhei Nishida, estudante de engenharia da Universidade Waseda, já tinha sido prata no salto com vara em Los Angeles, em 1932. Em Berlim, quatro anos depois, empatou com o amigo e companheiro de equipe Sueo Oe. Os dois não quiseram saltar um contra o outro para decidir quem ficava com qual medalha, e a própria delegação japonesa resolveu a questão: Nishida levou a prata e Oe, o bronze, com o critério de que Nishida tinha passado a altura com menos tentativas. A disputa aparece numa cena de Olympia, o documentário de Leni Riefenstahl sobre aqueles Jogos. De volta ao Japão, os dois pediram a um joalheiro que cortasse as duas medalhas e emendasse as partes, formando duas novas peças, metade prata e metade bronze, que ficaram conhecidas como "medalhas da amizade". Nishida seguiu no esporte a vida toda: aos 41 anos ganhou um bronze nos Jogos Asiáticos de 1951, foi árbitro e dirigente, e em 1989 recebeu a Ordem Olímpica em prata.

fontes.trecho: He was a student of the Engineering Department at Waseda University, when selected as a member of the Japanese Olympic team for the 1932 Summer Olympics in Los Angeles, where he won the silver medal in the pole vault event. [...] He subsequently participated in the 1936 Summer Olympics held in Berlin, Germany where he repeated his performance winning a second silver medal in the same event tying with his friend and teammate Sueo Oe. When the two declined to compete against each other to decide a winner, Nishida was awarded the silver and Oe the bronze by decision of the Japanese team, on the basis that Nishida had cleared the height in fewer attempts. The competition was featured in a scene in the documentary Olympia, filmed by Leni Riefenstahl. On their return to Japan, Nishida and Oe famously had their Olympic medals cut in half, and had a jeweler splice together two new “friendship medals”, half in bronze and half in silver. At the age of 41, Nishida won a bronze medal at the 1951 Asian Games. He remained active in sports all of his life, serving as a referee at events, and from 1959 as an honorary vice chairman of the Japan Association of Athletics Federations, and as a member of the Japanese Olympic Committee. In 1989, he was awarded the silver medal of the Olympic Order.

gancho: A primeira americana campeã olímpica, Margaret Abbott, venceu um torneio de golfe em Paris, em 1900, sem saber que era Olimpíada. Morreu em 1955 sem nunca ter descoberto.
explicacao: A Olimpíada de 1900 se misturou à Exposição Universal de Paris e se espalhou de maio a outubro, sem cerimônia de abertura nem de encerramento. Foi também a primeira com mulheres: 22 entre 997 atletas. Muitas provas nem eram anunciadas como olímpicas; o golfe feminino aparecia como "competição da Exposição", e o historiador Bill Mallon diz que muitos atletas não sabiam que estavam numa Olimpíada. Abbott, uma americana que estudava arte em Paris, soube do torneio por um anúncio de jornal e se inscreveu junto com a mãe. A prova tinha 9 buracos; ela venceu com 47 tacadas, e a mãe empatou em sétimo. O prêmio foi uma tigela de porcelana, já que o golfe não deu medalhas. Mais tarde, segundo o filho, ela dizia ter ganhado porque as francesas tinham entendido mal o tipo de jogo e aparecido de salto alto e saia justa. A façanha só veio à tona décadas depois, quando Paula Welch, professora da Universidade da Flórida, pesquisou a vida dela; em 2018, o jornal The New York Times publicou seu obituário, atrasado.

fontes.trecho: She was the first American woman to win an Olympic event: the women's golf tournament at the 1900 Summer Olympics. [...] In 1899, she traveled with her mother to Paris to study art. The following year, along with her mother, she signed up for a women's golf tournament without realizing that it was the second modern Olympics. Abbott won the tournament with a score of 47 strokes; her mother tied for seventh place. Abbott received a porcelain bowl as a prize. [...] Abbott died at the age of 76 in 1955, never realizing that she won an Olympic event. She was not well known until Paula Welch, a professor at the University of Florida, researched her life. In 2018, The New York Times published her belated obituary. [...] The 1900 Summer Olympics, hosted in Paris between May and October, was the second modern Olympics. [...] In 1900, however, women were allowed to compete for the first time in five sports: golf, tennis, sailing, rowing and equestrianism. Out of a total of 997 athletes, 22 were women. The events lacked proper equipment, did not have an opening or closing ceremony [...] The women's event was held over 9 holes [...] The Olympics coincided with the 1900 Paris Exposition [...] The golf tournament was billed as the "Exposition Competition" or "Paris World's Fair Competition" instead of being referred to as an Olympic event. [...] According to Mallon, many athletes did not know that they were participating in the Olympics. Abbott learned about the tournament from a newspaper notice. [...] According to Philip Dunne, his mother would later tell her family she won the tournament "because all the French girls apparently misunderstood the nature of the game scheduled that day and turned up to play in high heels and tight skirts". [...] No medals were awarded for many other events, including golf

gancho: Semanas depois de a URSS esmagar a Revolução Húngara, Hungria e URSS se enfrentaram no polo aquático da Olimpíada de 1956. O jogo foi tão violento que a polícia entrou para evitar um tumulto na torcida.
explicacao: A rivalidade já vinha de antes: com o controle político sobre a Hungria, os soviéticos tinham estudado e copiado os métodos de treino dos húngaros, campeões olímpicos. Em outubro de 1956, um protesto de estudantes em Budapeste virou revolta, e em novembro tanques soviéticos esmagaram o levante. A seleção húngara treinava nas montanhas acima da cidade e ouvia os tiros. Foi levada à Tchecoslováquia e só soube da dimensão da repressão ao chegar à Austrália. Na semifinal de 6 de dezembro, os húngaros tinham um plano: provocar os rivais em russo, língua que haviam aprendido na escola. Houve chutes e socos desde o início. Com um minuto para o fim e a Hungria vencendo por 4 a 0, o soviético Valentin Prokopov acertou Ervin Zádor, que saiu da piscina sangrando acima do olho. Torcedores furiosos desceram até a beira da piscina, os juízes encerraram a partida e a Hungria foi declarada vencedora. As fotos deram ao jogo o nome de "Sangue na água", embora a história de que a água ficou vermelha seja exagero. A Hungria levou o ouro, e depois Zádor e alguns colegas desertaram para o Ocidente.

fontes.trecho: was a water polo match between Hungary and the USSR at the 1956 Melbourne Olympics. The semi-final match took place on 6 December 1956 against the background of the recent Hungarian Revolution, and saw Hungary defeat the USSR 4–0. The name was coined after Hungarian player Ervin Zádor emerged during the last two minutes with blood pouring from above his eye after being punched by Soviet player Valentin Prokopov. Tensions were at an all-time high between the competing teams; the Soviet armed forces had violently suppressed the Hungarian Revolution just weeks before. [...] the Soviets had taken advantage of their political control of Hungary to study and copy the training methods and tactics of the Olympic champion Hungarians. Then, on 23 October 1956, a demonstration by students of the Budapest University of Technology and Economics escalated into an uprising against the government in Budapest. On 1 November, Soviet tanks started rolling into Hungary and from 4 to 10 November forces began suppressing the uprising [...] At the time, the Hungarian water polo team was in a mountain training camp above Budapest. They were able to hear the gunfire and see smoke rising. [...] they were moved into Czechoslovakia to avoid being caught in the revolution. The players only learned of the true extent of the uprising and the subsequent crackdown after arriving in Australia [...] The Hungarians had created a strategy before the game to taunt the Soviets, whose language they had studied in school. [...] From the beginning, kicks and punches were exchanged. [...] With one minute remaining in the match, Hungary was leading 4–0. [...] Prokopov struck him, causing a bleeding gash. Zádor left the pool; his bleeding was the final straw for a crowd already in a frenzy. Many angry spectators jumped onto the concourse beside the water, shook their fists, shouted abuse and spat at the Russians. To avoid a riot, police entered the arena and shepherded the crowd away. Pictures of Zádor's injuries were then published by newspapers, leading to the "Blood in the Water" moniker. Reports that the water in the pool turned red were, however, an exaggeration. [...] The referees stopped the match; Hungary was declared the winner since they had been leading. Hungary then beat Yugoslavia 2–1 in the final to win their fourth Olympic gold medal. Zádor's injury forced him to miss the match. After the event was completed, he and some of his teammates defected to the West.

gancho: Na final olímpica de basquete de 1972, os três segundos finais foram jogados três vezes, até a URSS virar sobre os EUA. Os americanos recusaram a prata, e as medalhas seguem guardadas num cofre na Suíça.
explicacao: Os Estados Unidos nunca tinham perdido um jogo olímpico de basquete: eram sete ouros seguidos desde 1936 e 63 vitórias a zero antes daquela final, em Munique, em plena Guerra Fria. Faltando três segundos, Doug Collins converteu dois lances livres e pôs os americanos na frente por 50 a 49. Durante o segundo arremesso, uma buzina soou na mesa: os soviéticos alegavam ter pedido tempo. O jogo foi interrompido com um segundo restando, e o secretário-geral da FIBA, Renato William Jones, desceu das arquibancadas e exigiu que os três segundos fossem repetidos. Na segunda tentativa, a buzina tocou e os americanos comemoraram, mas o relógio não tinha sido ajustado, e a jogada foi refeita mais uma vez. Na terceira, um árbitro fez um gesto ao americano Tom McMillen, que se afastou de Ivan Edeshko; livre, Edeshko lançou a bola de uma ponta à outra da quadra, e Alexander Belov pegou e fez a cesta da vitória quando a buzina soou de vez. O protesto americano foi rejeitado por um júri de cinco membros, três deles de países aliados da URSS, numa votação que não foi unânime. Os jogadores votaram, por unanimidade, recusar as medalhas, e o COI exige o aceite de todo o time para entregá-las.

fontes.trecho: The final three seconds of the game were played three times under questionable rule interpretations, leading to an ultimate victory by the Soviet team. [...] was among the contenders to win another in Munich at the 1972 Summer Olympics. [...] Since the first Olympic basketball tournament at the 1936 Olympics in Berlin, the Americans had not lost a single game, winning seven consecutive gold medals in dominating fashion. Their record reached an unprecedented 63–0 before the final game. [...] The United States and Soviet Union sporting rivalry reached its peak during the Cold War. [...] With three seconds remaining on the game clock, Collins was awarded two free throws and sank the first to tie the score at 49. Just as Collins lifted the ball to begin his shooting motion in attempting the second free throw, the horn from the scorer's table sounded [...] scoring to put the U.S. ahead by a score of 50–49. [...] He asserted that head coach Vladimir Kondrashin had called for a time-out [...] The game clock was stopped with one second remaining. [...] Renato William Jones, the secretary general of FIBA at the time [...] ruling that the entire inbounds sequence would be replayed from the point immediately following the second free throw and that the game clock would thus be reset to three seconds. Jones, who had had a contentious relationship with American basketball officials for a number of years, came down from the stands to the court to contribute to the officials' ruling, and he insisted upon a complete replay of the final three seconds. [...] not noticing that clock operator Andre Chopard was still working on getting the game clock set to three seconds. [...] the U.S. team began a joyful celebration of its apparent one-point victory. [...] the officials once again ordered the court to be cleared, the players to be brought back into position, the clock to be reset, and the final three seconds be replayed. [...] On the third inbound try, McMillen was again assigned to use his height to challenge Edeshko's inbound pass. However, as official Artenik Arabadjian prepared to put the ball into play, he gestured to McMillen. McMillen responded by backing several feet away from Edeshko, which gave Edeshko a clear view and unobstructed path to throw a long pass down the court. [...] Belov caught the ball in the air [...] Belov then gathered himself and made an uncontested layup, scoring the winning points as the horn sounded for the last time. [...] filed a detailed protest, which was heard by FIBA's five-member jury of appeal. [...] In announcing the verdict, Hepp steadfastly refused to provide the specifics of the vote count, acknowledging only that the decision was not unanimous. With three of the five jury members, including Hepp, being from Soviet-allied nations [...] the U.S. players did not accept the jury's verdict, voting unanimously to refuse their silver medals, and the team did not attend the medal ceremony. The silver medals are still kept in a vault in Lausanne, Switzerland. [...] With regard to awarding the medals, the IOC has insisted that for such an action, the entire team would need to consent unanimously.

gancho: Na foto do protesto de 1968, o australiano Peter Norman, prata na prova, usava um broche de apoio. E foi ideia dele que Smith e Carlos dividissem um par de luvas pretas, uma para cada um.
explicacao: Na final dos 200 metros na Cidade do México, o americano Tommie Smith venceu com recorde mundial, 19,83 segundos, e Norman passou John Carlos na chegada para levar a prata com 20,06 segundos, marca que seguiu como recorde da Oceania por mais de 56 anos. Depois da prova, Smith e Carlos contaram a Norman o que pretendiam fazer no pódio. Segundo o jornalista Martin Flanagan, perguntaram se ele acreditava em direitos humanos e, diante do sim, ouviram: "Eu fico com vocês". A caminho da cerimônia, Norman pediu emprestado a um remador americano, Paul Hoffman, o broche do Projeto Olímpico pelos Direitos Humanos. Como Carlos tinha esquecido as luvas na Vila Olímpica, Norman sugeriu que os dois dividissem o par de Smith; por isso Smith ergueu o punho direito e Carlos, o esquerdo. Muito se escreveu que Norman virou pária na Austrália e foi barrado em 1972, mas o Comitê Olímpico Australiano sustenta que ele não cumpriu os critérios de seleção, e o tema segue em debate. Quando Norman morreu, em 2006, Smith e Carlos fizeram discursos e carregaram o caixão.

fontes.trecho: He won the silver medal in the 200 metres at the 1968 Summer Olympics in Mexico City, with a time of 20.06 seconds, which remained the Oceania 200 m record for more than 56 years. [...] He knew the salute was to occur and wore a badge of the Olympic Project for Human Rights in support of fellow athletes John Carlos and Tommie Smith. [...] On the morning of 16 October, US athlete Tommie Smith won the 200-metre final with a world-record time of 19.83 seconds. Norman finished second in a time of 20.06 s after passing U.S. athlete John Carlos at the finish line. [...] Norman died of a heart attack on 3 October 2006 in Melbourne at the age of 64. [...] both Smith and Carlos gave eulogies and were pallbearers at Norman's funeral. [...] After the final, Carlos and Smith had told Norman what they were planning to do during the ceremony. Journalist Martin Flanagan wrote: "They asked Norman if he believed in human rights. He said he did. [...] He said, 'I'll stand with you'. [...] On the way to the medal ceremony, Norman saw the OPHR badge being worn by Paul Hoffman, a white member of the US rowing team, and asked him if he could wear it. It was Norman who suggested that Smith and Carlos share the black gloves used in their salute, after Carlos left his pair at the Olympic Village. This is the reason Smith raised a gloved right fist and Carlos raised his gloved left. [...] he returned home to Australia a pariah, suffering unofficial sanction and ridicule as the Black Power salute's forgotten man. [...] Various commentators say he was not selected for the Olympic Games in Munich in 1972 despite recording qualifying times, but the Australian Olympic Committee maintains that Norman was not selected for the 1972 Olympics because he did not meet the selection standard

gancho: Em 1938, uma granada defeituosa feriu gravemente a mão direita do atirador húngaro Károly Takács. Ele treinou escondido com a esquerda e foi campeão olímpico de pistola de tiro rápido em 1948 e 1952.
explicacao: Em 1936, Takács já estava entre os melhores do mundo na pistola, mas ficou fora da equipe húngara para Berlim porque era sargento, e só oficiais podiam competir. A regra caiu depois daqueles Jogos, e ele mirava a Olimpíada de 1940, marcada para Tóquio. Em 1938, durante um treinamento do exército, uma granada defeituosa explodiu e feriu gravemente sua mão direita. Takács decidiu continuar e passou a atirar com a esquerda, treinando em segredo; na primavera de 1939, surpreendeu o país ao vencer o campeonato húngaro, e no mesmo ano fez parte da equipe campeã mundial. As Olimpíadas de 1940 e 1944 foram canceladas pela Segunda Guerra. Em Londres, em 1948, aos 38 anos, ele venceu o favorito, o argentino Carlos Enrique Díaz Sáenz Valiente, então campeão mundial, e em Helsinque, em 1952, ganhou de novo. Foi o primeiro atirador a conquistar dois ouros na pistola de tiro rápido de 25 metros. Ainda competiu em Melbourne, em 1956, mas terminou em oitavo.

fontes.trecho: was the first shooter to win two Olympic gold medals in the 25 metre rapid fire pistol event, both with his left hand after his right hand was seriously injured. [...] By 1936, he was a world-class pistol shooter, but he was denied a place in the Hungarian shooting team for the 1936 Summer Olympics on the grounds that he was a sergeant, and only commissioned officers were allowed to compete. This prohibition was lifted in Hungary after the Berlin Games, and Takács had expectations of success at the 1940 Summer Olympics, scheduled to be held in Tokyo. During army training in 1938, his right hand was badly injured when a faulty grenade exploded. Takács was determined to continue his shooting career, and switched to shooting with his left hand. He practiced in secret, surprising his countrymen when he won the Hungarian national pistol shooting championship in the spring of 1939. He also was a member of the Hungarian team that won the 1939 UIT World Shooting Championships in the event. [...] The Olympic Games scheduled for 1940 and 1944 were canceled due to the Second World War. However, Takács surprised the world by winning the gold medal at the 1948 Summer Olympics in London, aged 38, beating the favourite, Argentine Carlos Enrique Díaz Sáenz Valiente, the reigning world champion. Takács won a second gold medal in the same event at the 1952 Summer Olympics in Helsinki [...] Takács also attended the 1956 Summer Olympics in Melbourne, but finished eighth and failed to win a third medal.

gancho: A explicação clássica para o patim deslizar, a pressão da lâmina derretendo o gelo, não fecha a conta: por ela, patinar abaixo de −4 °C seria impossível. Por que o gelo escorrega ainda é estudado.
explicacao: A ideia do derretimento por pressão vem do século XIX: a lâmina, apertando o gelo, formaria uma película de água que lubrificaria o deslizamento. Em 1939, Frank Bowden e T. P. Hughes mostraram que, se fosse só isso, os patinadores sentiriam muito mais atrito do que sentem. E há o problema da temperatura: o gelo ideal para a patinação artística fica por volta de −5,5 °C, e o do hóquei, de −9 °C, abaixo do limite que essa teoria permitiria. Bowden e Hughes propuseram então que o calor do próprio atrito derrete uma camada fina, o que não explica por que o gelo escorrega mesmo para quem está parado sobre ele. Outra proposta diz que as moléculas da superfície se ligam mal às de baixo e formam uma camada quase líquida, que lubrifica independentemente da pressão. Experimentos com microscopia de força atômica, porém, contestam o peso dessa camada. Um estudo de 2014 sugere que o aquecimento por atrito é o processo mais importante na maioria das situações comuns, mas o mecanismo que controla o atrito do gelo continua sendo pesquisado.

fontes.trecho: This subject was first scientifically investigated in the 19th century. The preferred explanation at the time was "pressure melting" – i.e. the blade of an ice skate, upon exerting pressure on the ice, would melt a thin layer, providing sufficient lubrication for the blade to glide across the ice. Yet, research in 1939 by Frank P. Bowden and T. P. Hughes found that skaters would experience a lot more friction than they actually do if it were the only explanation. Further, the optimum temperature for figure skating is −5.5 °C (22 °F; 268 K) and −9 °C (16 °F; 264 K) for ice hockey; yet, according to pressure melting theory, skating below −4 °C (25 °F; 269 K) would be outright impossible. Instead, Bowden and Hughes argued that heating and melting of the ice layer is caused by friction. However, this theory does not sufficiently explain why ice is slippery when standing still even at below-zero temperatures. Subsequent research suggested that ice molecules at the interface cannot properly bond with the molecules of the mass of ice beneath (and thus are free to move like molecules of liquid water). These molecules remain in a semi-liquid state, providing lubrication regardless of pressure against the ice exerted by any object. However, the significance of this hypothesis is disputed by experiments showing a high coefficient of friction for ice using atomic force microscopy. Thus, the mechanism controlling the frictional properties of ice is still an active area of scientific study. [...] Research in 2014 suggests that frictional heating is the most important process under most typical conditions.

It had long been believed that ice is slippery because the pressure of an object in contact with it causes a thin layer to melt. The hypothesis was that the blade of an ice skate, exerting pressure on the ice, melts a thin layer, providing lubrication between the ice and the blade. This explanation, called "pressure melting", originated in the 19th century.

gancho: Um copo emborcado que desliza girando no sentido horário curva para a esquerda. A pedra de curling, girando igual, curva para a direita, e os físicos ainda não chegaram a um acordo sobre o porquê.
explicacao: No copo, a explicação é conhecida: ao deslizar, ele se inclina um pouco para a frente, a borda dianteira aperta mais a mesa e freia mais, e o copo desvia para o lado desse atrito maior. Por muito tempo se supôs que a pedra fazia o contrário por um motivo parecido: a pressão maior na frente derreteria um pouco o gelo, e o atrito mais forte ficaria atrás. Em 2012, uma equipe da Universidade de Uppsala, na Suécia, fez as contas e viu que isso não basta. A pedra gira devagar, só umas duas voltas até parar, pouco demais para desviar um metro ou mais, e o desvio pode chegar a um metro e meio. Pior: girar mais não aumenta a curva, e girar demais a elimina. Com um microscópio eletrônico, os suecos acharam riscos minúsculos deixados pela borda da frente, que serviriam de guia para a borda de trás. Riscando o gelo de propósito, eles conseguiram até fazer uma pedra andar em zigue-zague. A proposta gerou controvérsia. Em 2020, uma equipe japonesa testou as teorias numa pista de curling, com rastreamento de movimento e microscópio a laser, e nenhuma saiu vencedora.

fontes.titulo: The slippery science of Olympic curling: we still don't know how it works (UNSW Sydney / The Conversation)
fontes.trecho: The game of curling is centuries old, but exactly what makes the stones curl as they slide over the ice is still a mystery. [...] Even a small amount of rotation can deflect the path of the curling stone by as much as a metre and a half. [...] you will be able to make the glass trace a curving path across the table, deflecting to the left when you spin it clockwise or to the right when you spin it anticlockwise. [...] When the spinning glass slides across the table, it leans forward slightly in the direction of travel, pushing the front lip of the glass down a little harder on the table than the trailing lip. The extra pressure generates extra friction at the front compared to the back. The resulting imbalance of friction forces causes the glass to deflect in the direction of stronger friction – to the left in the case of a clockwise-rotating glass. [...] But curling stones behave in exactly the opposite way: a clockwise rotation causes the stone to deflect to the right, not the left. For a long time, scientists assumed this was because of an effect called asymmetrical friction. [...] The extra pressure at the front of the stone partially melts the ice at the leading edge, creating a thin film of water that reduces the friction at the front of stone compared with the back. [...] In 2012, a team at Uppsala University in Sweden made detailed calculations of the friction forces acting on a sliding stone. The problem they found is that curling stones rotate quite slowly, only completing a couple of turns before coming to a stop. This spin is far too small to cause a sideways deflection of a metre or more. Even odder, more rotation does not lead to more curl – in fact, spin a stone too hard and it won’t curl at all. [...] The researchers used an electron microscope to look more closely at the ice under a curling stone. They discovered that the front edge of the stone leaves behind miniscule scratches on the ice in the direction of rotation. These scratches act as a guide for the back edge of the stone, causing the stone to deflect in the direction of rotation. [...] In one experiment, a stone was made to travel along a zigzag path by laying down scratches in alternating directions. Their findings ignited a minor controversy in the admittedly niche world of curling physics. [...] In 2020, a Japanese team attempted to clear things up by systematically testing each theory in a curling hall using sophisticated motion-tracking equipment, a laser scanning microscope [...] However, no clear winner emerged.

gancho: O recorde do dardo chegou a 104,80 m, e lançamentos acima de 100 m já ameaçavam a segurança dentro do estádio. Em 1986, o dardo foi redesenhado para voar menos: o centro de gravidade avançou 4 cm.
explicacao: Por muito tempo, os dardos foram de madeira maciça com ponta de aço. Nos anos 1950 surgiu o modelo oco e aerodinâmico do americano Bud Held, que voava mais longe, mas também caía de chapado com mais frequência, o que gerava discussões e protestos sobre a validade dos lançamentos. O recorde mundial chegou aos 104,80 m de Uwe Hohn, e em 1º de abril de 1986 a federação internacional de atletismo mudou o dardo masculino. Além de levar o centro de gravidade 4 cm para a frente, o modelo novo tem menos área antes desse ponto e mais área depois, como as penas de uma flecha. O dardo tende a se alinhar com o vento relativo, e na descida esse vento parece vir do chão: ele vira a ponta para baixo. Assim, gera menos sustentação e perde cerca de 10% de distância, mas crava no chão com muito mais regularidade. Os recordes foram zerados. Em 2017, o melhor lançamento com o dardo novo ainda era o de Jan Železný, de 1996, com 98,48 m. O dardo feminino passou pela mesma mudança em 1999.

fontes.trecho: For a long time, javelins were made of solid wood, typically birch, with a steel tip. The hollow, highly aerodynamic Held javelin, invented by American thrower Bud Held and developed and manufactured by his brother Dick, was introduced in the 1950s [...] These new javelins flew further, but were also less likely to land neatly point first [...] became official for men starting in April 1986 and for women in April 1999, and the world records (then 104.80 m by Uwe Hohn, and 80.00 m by Petra Felke) were reset. The current (as of 2017) men's world record is held by Jan Železný at 98.48 m (1996) [...] On 1 April 1986, the men's javelin (800 grams (1.76 lb)) was redesigned by the governing body (the IAAF Technical Committee). They decided to change the rules for javelin design because of the increasingly frequent flat landings and the resulting discussions and protests when these attempts were declared valid or invalid by competition judges. The world record had also crept up to a potentially dangerous level, 104.80 m (343.8 ft) by Uwe Hohn. With throws exceeding 100 metres, it was becoming difficult to safely stage the competition within the confines of a stadium infield. The javelin was redesigned so that the centre of gravity was moved 4 cm (1.6 in) forward. In addition, the surface area in front of centre of gravity was reduced, while the surface area behind the centre of gravity was increased. This had an effect similar to that produced by the feathers on an arrow. The javelin turns into the relative wind. This relative wind appears to originate from the ground as the javelin descends, thus the javelin turns to face the ground. As the javelin turns into the wind less lift is generated, reducing the flight distance by around 10% but also causing the javelin to stick in the ground more consistently. In 1999, the women's javelin (600 grams (1.32 lb)) was similarly redesigned.

gancho: Abrir os esquis em V fez os saltadores de esqui irem cerca de 10% mais longe. Mas também tornou vantajoso ser muito leve, e a federação passou a punir os magros demais com esquis mais curtos.
explicacao: Até meados dos anos 1960, os saltadores desciam a rampa com os dois braços apontados para a frente, e durante décadas o voo foi feito com os esquis paralelos. Nos anos 1980, o sueco Jan Boklöv abriu caminho para o estilo em V, hoje usado por praticamente todos. Com ele, os saltadores passam a distância de referência da rampa em cerca de 10% a mais do que com a técnica anterior. A mudança deu mais importância ao tempo no ar em relação ao impulso da decolagem, e ter pouquíssimo peso virou vantagem. Vieram casos de anorexia, e em meados dos anos 1990 já se falava de treinadores pressionando atletas a emagrecer. Em 2004, a Federação Internacional de Esqui criou uma regra: quem tem índice de massa corporal abaixo de 20 (hoje, 21) é obrigado a usar esquis mais curtos, que geram menos sustentação. A regra é creditada por acabar com os casos mais graves, mas sua eficácia é muitas vezes questionada, porque o esqui encurtado pode ser compensado com ainda menos peso e com fixações modernas. Dezenas de saltadores e treinadores, atuais e antigos, já criticaram o problema em público.

fontes.trecho: The jumping technique has evolved over the years, from jumps with the skis parallel and both arms extended forward, to the "V-style", which is widely used today. [...] Ski jumpers below the minimum safe body mass index are penalised with a shorter maximum ski length, reducing the aerodynamic lift they can achieve. These rules have been credited with stopping the most severe cases of underweight athletes, but some competitors still lose weight to maximise the distance they can achieve. [...] By using the V-style, firstly pioneered by Swedish ski jumper Jan Boklöv in the mid-1980s, modern skiers are able to exceed the distance of the take-off hill by about 10% compared to the previous technique with parallel skis. [...] Until the mid-1960s, the ski jumper came down the in-run of the hill with both arms pointing forwards. [...] After the V-style was established, the period of flying became more relevant in relation to the take-off. It became advantageous for ski jumpers to have a very low body weight. The problem was first publicized by Stephan Zünd, who suffered from anorexia nervosa. [...] In late 1996 Dieter Thoma talked in an interview about trainers putting athletes under pressure to gain a low body weight. In 2004 the FIS announced a new rule which requires the length of an athletes skis to be shortened when an athlete has a BMI under 20 (today under 21). [...] The rule's efficacy is often doubted, because the cut ski can be compensated with a low body weight and modern ski bindings. Current and former ski jumpers, who have talked critically about the topic, include
He is best known for popularising the now-ubiquitous V-style in the late 1980s and early 1990s.

gancho: As covinhas da bola de golfe nasceram de uma observação: bolas velhas, marcadas pelo uso, iam mais longe que as novas e lisas. A rugosidade muda o ar junto à bola e diminui o arrasto.
explicacao: A partir de 1848, as bolas passaram a ser feitas de guta-percha, a seiva seca de uma árvore da Malásia, moldada a quente. Por acaso, descobriu-se que os cortes deixados pelo uso davam a elas um voo mais regular que o de uma bola perfeitamente lisa, e os fabricantes passaram a marcar a superfície de propósito, com faca ou com martelo e cinzel. Em 1905, o engenheiro inglês William Taylor, que percebera que os jogadores tentavam deixar as bolas irregulares porque as usadas iam mais longe, patenteou um padrão de covinhas depois de testes sistemáticos. A física explica a vantagem. As covinhas tornam turbulenta a fina camada de ar que envolve a frente da bola, e essa camada turbulenta continua grudada à superfície por mais tempo. Com isso, a esteira de baixa pressão atrás da bola fica mais estreita, e o arrasto cai. Além disso, quando a bola gira para trás, as covinhas aumentam a sustentação criada pelo efeito Magnus. Hoje as bolas costumam ter de 300 a 500 covinhas, e as regras exigem que o desenho seja simétrico.

fontes.trecho: In 1848, the Rev. Dr. Robert Adams Paterson (sometimes spelled Patterson) invented the gutta-percha ball (or guttie, gutty). The guttie was made from dried sap of the Malaysian sapodilla tree. The sap had a rubber-like feel and could be made spherical by heating and shaping it in a mold. [...] Accidentally, it was discovered that nicks in the guttie from normal use actually provided a ball with a more consistent ball flight than a guttie with a perfectly smooth surface. Thus, makers began intentionally making indentations into the surface of new balls using either a knife or hammer and chisel [...] Dimpled balls fly farther than non-dimpled balls due to the combination of these two effects. First, the dimples on the surface of a golf ball cause the boundary layer on the upstream side of the ball to transition from laminar to turbulent. The turbulent boundary layer is able to remain attached to the surface of the ball much longer than a laminar boundary with fewer eddies and so creates a narrower low-pressure wake and hence less pressure drag. [...] Second, backspin generates lift by deforming the airflow around the ball, in a similar manner to an airplane wing. This is called the Magnus effect. The dimples on a golf ball deform the air around the ball quickly causing a turbulent airflow that results in more Magnus lift than a smooth ball would experience. [...] Dimples first became a feature of golf balls when English engineer and manufacturer William Taylor, co-founder of the Taylor-Hobson company, registered a patent for a dimple design in 1905. William Taylor had realized that golf players were trying to make irregularities on their balls, noticing that used balls were going further than new ones. Hence he decided to make systematic tests to determine what surface formation would give the best flight. [...] Most modern golf balls have about 300–500 dimples [...] Officially sanctioned balls are designed to be as symmetrical as possible.

gancho: Na Olimpíada de Pequim, em 2008, 94% das provas de natação foram vencidas com o mesmo maiô, o LZR Racer, que comprimia o corpo e prendia ar. Em 2010, maiôs de corpo inteiro foram proibidos.
explicacao: O LZR Racer foi lançado pela Speedo em fevereiro de 2008. Feito de elastano, náilon e poliuretano, foi desenvolvido com o Instituto Australiano do Esporte e com apoio de túneis de vento da NASA. Ele reduzia em 24% o arrasto do atrito com a água em relação ao maiô anterior da marca, e estudos iniciais sugeriram tempos 1,9% a 2,2% menores. Ao apertar o corpo e prender ar, o traje também dava flutuação, e houve quem usasse dois maiôs ou mais, um sobre o outro, para ampliar o efeito. Em Pequim, 98% das medalhas da natação e 23 dos 25 recordes mundiais quebrados saíram com ele. Nadadores japoneses, presos a contratos com outras marcas, ficaram em desvantagem até a federação do país liberar a escolha do traje. Logo surgiu a expressão "doping tecnológico". Em março de 2009, a FINA limitou o comprimento e a espessura dos maiôs e, em julho, numa virada brusca, votou quase por unanimidade proibir todos os de corpo inteiro. Desde janeiro de 2010, só vale tecido, e os maiôs vão no máximo da cintura ao joelho, para os homens, e do ombro ao joelho, para as mulheres.

fontes.trecho: The LZR Racer (pronounced as "Laser Racer") is a line of competition swimsuits manufactured by Speedo using a high-technology swimwear fabric composed of woven elastane-nylon and polyurethane. The swimsuits are available in a full-body length; they compress the body and trap air for buoyancy. The LZR Pro and LZR Elite were launched on 13 February 2008 [...] The LZR Pro and LZR Elite were developed by Mectex, an Italian company, in association with the Australian Institute of Sport, with the help of Speedo's sponsored athletes. NASA's wind tunnel testing facilities and fluid flow analysis software supported the design. [...] The design result, called the LZR Racer, reduced skin friction drag by 24% compared to the previous Speedo swimsuit. [...] early case studies suggested that the LZR Elite was effective in reducing the racing times of competitive swimmers by 1.9 to 2.2 percent. [...] The LZR Racer's impact extended to the Beijing Olympics, where 94% of all swimming races were won in the suit. 98% of all swimming medals won and 23 of the 25 world records broken at the Beijing Olympics were won by swimmers wearing the suit. [...] A problem arose for the Japanese Olympic swimmers, who had exclusive contracts with swimsuit makers Mizuno, Asics, and Descente, preventing them from wearing the Speedo brand suits in the Olympics. The Japanese Swimming Federation subsequently decided to allow its athletes to choose their own suits freely. [...] The combined effects of the LZR both compressing the body and trapping air for buoyancy led to many competitors who used the LZR wearing two or more suits for an increased effect. This led to some claiming that the LZR was in effect "technological doping". At its meeting in Dubai in March 2009, FINA stipulated that swimsuits should not cover the neck, must not extend past the shoulders and ankles, and also limit the suits' thickness and buoyancy. [...] In an abrupt reversal of opinion, the FINA Congress, which was held in Rome on 24 July 2009, during the 2009 World Aquatics Championships, voted almost unanimously to revert its previous policy and ban all body-length swimsuits. Men's swimsuits may maximally cover the area from the waist to the knee, and women's counterparts from the shoulder to the knee. They also ruled that the fabric used must be a "textile", that is, consisting natural or synthetic yarns woven together. [...] The new regulations took effect on 1 January 2010.

gancho: No atletismo de elite, reagir ao tiro de largada em menos de 0,1 s conta como largada falsa. Um estudo dos Jogos de 2008 indicou que o sensor, calibrado igual para todos, deixava mulheres saírem antes sem punição.
explicacao: A regra se baseia em testes segundo os quais o cérebro humano não consegue ouvir e processar o som da largada em menos de 0,1 segundo, embora um estudo encomendado pela federação, em 2009, tenha indicado que velocistas de ponta às vezes reagem em 0,08 segundo. Sensores nos blocos de partida medem a força dos pés: se ela passa de um limiar antes de 100 milissegundos após o tiro, é largada falsa, e hoje a primeira largada falsa já pode desclassificar o atleta. Pesquisadores da Universidade de Michigan analisaram as reações de 224 velocistas homens e 201 mulheres nos Jogos de Pequim. Com 99,9% de confiança, concluíram, ninguém reage em 100 ms, mas os homens chegam a 109 ms e as mulheres, a 121 ms. Essa diferença, porém, seria um artefato: com menos força muscular, elas demoram mais a atingir o mesmo limiar, e uma mulher poderia largar até 21 ms antes sem punição. Pelas contas dos autores, um limiar 22% menor para elas igualaria os tempos. Um estudo posterior, com os Jogos de 2004 a 2016, viu os tempos mínimos de reação caírem, e a diferença entre os sexos sumir em 2012. A explicação mais provável, segundo os autores, é a redução dos limiares, e não um treino melhor.

fontes.trecho: In track and field sprints, the sport's governing body, World Athletics, has a rule that if the athlete moves within 0.1 seconds after the gun has fired the athlete has false-started. This figure is based on tests that show the human brain cannot hear and process the information from the start sound in under 0.10 seconds, even though a IAAF-commissioned study indicated in 2009 that top sprinters are able to sometimes react in 0.08 seconds. [...] Since 2009, the offending athletes risk immediate disqualification.

fontes.titulo: Lipps, Galecki e Ashton-Miller (2011). On the Implications of a Sex Difference in the Reaction Times of Sprinters at the Beijing Olympics. PLoS ONE (Europe PMC)
fontes.trecho: Currently, a false start is awarded if an athlete increases the force on their starting block above a given threshold before 100 ms has elapsed after the starting gun. [...] At the 99.9% confidence level, neither men nor women can react in 100 ms, but they can react in as little as 109 ms and 121 ms, respectively. However, that sex difference in reaction time is likely an artifact caused by using the same force threshold in women as men, and it permits a woman to false start by up to 21 ms without penalty. We estimate that female sprinters would have similar reaction times to male sprinters if the force threshold used at Beijing was lowered by 22% in order to account for their lesser muscle strength. [...] Department of Biomedical Engineering, University of Michigan [...] Data were collected for 224 male sprinters (439 total male races) and 201 female sprinters (387 total female races)

fontes.titulo: On the apparent decrease in Olympic sprinter reaction times (2018). PLoS ONE (Europe PMC)
fontes.trecho: The results for the 100 m and 110 m hurdle events show that minimum reaction times have systematically decreased between 2004 and 2016 for both sexes, with women showing a marked decrease since 2008 that eliminated the sex difference in 2012. Because overall race times have not systematically decreased between 2004 and 2016, the most likely explanation for the apparent decrease in reaction times is a reduction in the proprietary force thresholds used to calculate the reaction times based on force sensors in starting blocks

gancho: O patim de lâmina articulada, patenteado já em 1894 e desprezado de início pelos melhores patinadores holandeses, provocou uma enxurrada de recordes na patinação de velocidade a partir da temporada 1996–1997.
explicacao: No patim tradicional, a lâmina é fixa na bota. No chamado clap skate, ela se prende só na frente, por uma dobradiça, e assim o patinador pode estender o tornozelo no fim da passada sem tirar a lâmina do gelo. A ideia é antiga: um patim articulado foi patenteado em 1894. O pesquisador holandês Gerrit Jan van Ingen Schenau, da Universidade Livre de Amsterdã, a reinventou a partir de 1979, apostando que a panturrilha poderia participar por mais tempo do movimento. Os grandes patinadores holandeses da época não se impressionaram. Na temporada 1994–1995, 11 jovens patinadores da Holanda do Sul usaram o patim e melhoraram seus tempos, em média, 6,25%, contra 2,5% dos colegas com patins comuns. Em 1996–1997, a seleção feminina holandesa o adotou com enorme sucesso, a campeã mundial alemã Gunda Niemann disse que ele deveria ser proibido, e o resto do mundo foi atrás. Caíram muitos recordes, inclusive nos Jogos de Inverno de Nagano, em 1998. Em 2000, um estudo do cientista do esporte holandês Han Houdijk e colegas, com dez patinadores de elite, apontou que o segredo está no ponto de rotação. No patim comum, o pé gira em torno da longa ponta da lâmina, e o impulso final é gerado de forma ineficaz. Com a dobradiça sob a base dos dedos, a extensão do tornozelo nos últimos 50 milissegundos da passada fica mais eficaz, e a velocidade subiu 5%.

fontes.trecho: Unlike in traditional skates where the blade is rigidly fixed to the boot, clap skates have the blade attached to the boot by a hinge at the front. This allows the blade to remain in contact with the ice longer, as the ankle can now be extended toward the end of the stroke [...] Clap skates were developed at the Faculty of Human Movement Sciences of the Vrije Universiteit of Amsterdam, led by Gerrit Jan van Ingen Schenau [...] In the 1996/1997 season, the Dutch women's team started using the skates with great success. The rest of the skating world soon followed suit, causing a torrent of world records to be broken in the following seasons, including the 1998 Winter Olympics in Nagano, Japan. [...] The idea of a hinging skate was described and patented in 1894 by Karl Hannes [...] It was re-invented by Gerrit Jan van Ingen Schenau, who started work on a hinged speed skate in 1979 [...] on the premise that a skater would benefit from the extended movement with the skate on the ice, allowing the calf muscles to longer partake in the skate movement. [...] The then current Dutch speed skating top professionals Ids Postma, Bart Veldkamp and Rintje Ritsma were unimpressed by the skate. For the 1994–1995 season, 11 skaters from the South Holland 14–18 age category started using the clap skate competitively. Those 11 showed an average improvement of 6.25% on their times, compared to 2.5% of the other skaters using regular speed skates. [...] leaving Gunda Niemann, the defending world champion, in second place. Niemann remarked that the skate was illegal, and should be outlawed. [...] Research completed in 2000 by Dutch sport scientist Han Houdijk showed that the speed gain from using the clap skate [...] the point of rotation is moved from the tip of the skate to the hinge, facilitating the transfer of power to the ice. [...] The clap skate was used first in the 1984/1985 skating season.

fontes.titulo: Houdijk et al. (2000). Push-off mechanics in speed skating with conventional skates and klapskates. Medicine & Science in Sports & Exercise (resumo, Europe PMC)
fontes.trecho: Ten elite speed skaters skated four 400-m laps at maximal effort with both conventional and klapskates. [...] Skating velocity increased 5% as a result of an increase in mean power output of 25 W when klapskates were used instead of conventional skates. [...] The difference in work per stroke occurs during the final 50 ms of the push-off. This is the result of the ineffective way in which push-off forces are generated with conventional skates when the foot rotates about the long front end of the blade. [...] A hinge under the ball of the foot enhances the effectiveness of plantar flexion during the final 50 ms of the push off with klapskates and increases work per stroke and mean power output.

gancho: A dor muscular do dia seguinte vem das contrações em que o músculo faz força enquanto se alonga; as de encurtamento não a causam. E o ácido lático, o suspeito de sempre, volta ao normal em até uma hora.
explicacao: Essa dor tardia aparece depois de exercícios puxados ou fora do costume e costuma ser mais forte entre 24 e 72 horas depois. Uma teoria antiga culpava o ácido lático, que continuaria sendo produzido após o treino e agiria como um resíduo tóxico. Ela foi amplamente rejeitada por dois motivos. Contrações em que o músculo se encurta também produzem ácido lático, mas não causam essa dor. E vários estudos mostram que o ácido lático volta aos níveis normais em até uma hora, muito antes de a dor começar. A explicação mais aceita aponta lesões microscópicas nas fibras, provocadas por contrações excêntricas, aquelas em que o músculo se alonga enquanto faz força. Exercícios estáticos causam bem menos dor, e os de encurtamento, nenhuma. A ideia de rupturas dentro do músculo já tinha sido proposta em 1902 por Theodore Hough. A dor também não é, necessariamente, um sinal para parar: exercícios durante esse período não pioraram a lesão nem atrasaram a recuperação nos estudos, embora uma segunda sessão excêntrica até uma semana depois tenha reduzido a força do músculo logo em seguida. E há um consolo: depois de uma sessão dolorida, o músculo se adapta rápido e passa a sofrer menos com o mesmo esforço, uma proteção que dura pelo menos várias semanas.

fontes.trecho: Delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS) is the pain and stiffness felt in muscles after unaccustomed or strenuous exercise. The soreness is felt most strongly 24 to 72 hours after the exercise. It is thought to be caused by eccentric (lengthening) exercise, which causes small-scale damage (microtrauma) to the muscle fibers. After such exercise, the muscle adapts rapidly to prevent muscle damage, and thereby soreness, if the exercise is repeated. [...] Muscle soreness is caused by eccentric exercise, that is, exercise consisting of eccentric (lengthening) contractions of the muscle. Isometric (static) exercise causes much less soreness, and concentric (shortening) exercise causes none. [...] DOMS was first described in 1902 by Theodore Hough, who concluded that this kind of soreness is "fundamentally the result of ruptures within the muscle". [...] An earlier theory posited that DOMS is connected to the build-up of lactic acid in the blood, which was thought to continue being produced following exercise. This build-up of lactic acid was thought to be a toxic metabolic waste product that caused the perception of pain at a delayed stage. This theory has been largely rejected, as concentric contractions which also produce lactic acid have been unable to cause DOMS. Additionally, lactic acid is known from multiple studies to return to normal levels within one hour of exercise, and therefore cannot cause the pain that occurs much later. [...] Furthermore, eccentric exercise during DOMS was found to not exacerbate muscle damage, nor did it have an adverse effect on recovery, indicating that soreness is not necessarily a warning sign to reduce the usage of the affected muscle. [...] Generally, though, the protective effect lasts for at least several weeks. [...] However, it was also observed that a second bout of eccentric exercise within one week of the initial exercise did lead to decreased muscle function immediately afterward.

gancho: O salto de costas, hoje usado por quase todos no salto em altura, foi desenvolvido quase ao mesmo tempo por Dick Fosbury, nos EUA, e pela canadense Debbie Brill. Os dois dependiam de uma novidade: o colchão de espuma.
explicacao: Saltar de costas já era conhecido, mas, enquanto o pouso era em areia, serragem ou lascas de madeira, o atleta precisava cair de pé ou apoiado nas mãos, como nas técnicas da tesoura e do rolo. No fim dos anos 1950, as universidades americanas passaram a usar blocos de espuma, bem mais macios e quase um metro mais altos, e no começo dos anos 1960 as escolas seguiram. Isso permitiu cair de costas com segurança. Fosbury desenvolveu o estilo no ensino médio, e em 1964 um jornal escreveu que ele parecia "um peixe se debatendo num barco"; outro o chamou de "o saltador em altura mais preguiçoso do mundo". No Canadá, Brill criou um estilo parecido ainda criança, num fosso com espuma que o pai fez na fazenda da família, e seus colegas de clube o achavam único até saberem de Fosbury. O ouro dele na Olimpíada de 1968, no México, mostrou o potencial da técnica. Arqueando o corpo sobre o sarrafo, o saltador mantém boa parte dele abaixo da barra, e o centro de massa pode, em teoria, passar por baixo dela. Dos 36 medalhistas olímpicos da prova entre 1972 e 2000, 34 usaram o salto de costas.

fontes.trecho: Though the backwards flop technique had been known for years before Fosbury, landing surfaces had been sandpits or low piles of matting and high jumpers had to land on their feet or at least land carefully to prevent injury. [...] While in flight, the athlete can progressively arch shoulders, back, and legs in a rolling motion, keeping as much of the body as possible below the bar. It is theoretically possible for the center of mass to pass under the bar.

He won a gold medal at the 1968 Summer Olympics, revolutionizing the high jump event with a "back-first" technique now known as the Fosbury flop. [...] Debbie Brill was developing her similar "Brill Bend" around the same time. [...] Sawdust, sand, or woodchip surfaces had been usable previously because jumpers using the scissors technique were able to clear the bar while upright and then land on their feet, and those using the Western Roll or Straddle made a three-point landing on their hands and lead leg. In the late 1950s, U.S. colleges began to use bundles of soft foam rubber, usually held together by a mesh net. These bundles were not only much softer, but raised the landing height about three feet (0.91 m) off the ground. By the early 1960s, U.S. high schools were following the lead of the colleges in acquiring foam rubber landing pits. With the softer, elevated landing surface, Fosbury was able to land safely. [...] The technique gained the name the "Fosbury Flop" when in 1964 the Medford Mail-Tribune ran a photo captioned "Fosbury Flops Over Bar," while in an accompanying article a reporter wrote that he looked like "a fish flopping in a boat." Others were even less kind, with one newspaper captioning Fosbury's photograph, "World's Laziest High Jumper". [...] Of the 36 Olympic medalists in the event from 1972 through 2000, 34 used "the Flop", making it the most popular technique in high jumping.

Her reverse jumping style—which is now almost exclusively the technique of elite high jumpers—was called the Brill Bend and was developed by her when she was a child, around the same time as Dick Fosbury was developing the similar Fosbury Flop in the US. [...] She developed her style of jumping as a preteen on the family farm when her father made a landing pit containing foam rubber. [...] Her clubmates thought it was unique until they learned that an older American athlete, Dick Fosbury, was becoming known for using the same technique.

gancho: No beisebol, a bola com efeito faz uma curva suave, mas os rebatedores dizem que ela "quebra" de repente perto da base. Uma hipótese de 2010: a visão periférica distorce o movimento de objetos que giram.
explicacao: Já se discutiu se a bola curva existia mesmo ou era ilusão de ótica. Em 1949, o engenheiro aeronáutico Ralph Lightfoot, da Sikorsky, usou túnel de vento para provar que ela curva de fato: o giro desequilibra as forças sobre a bola, que segue um caminho suave e parabólico. O enigma passou a ser outro: por que os rebatedores relatam uma mudança quase descontínua de posição perto da base? Em 2010, pesquisadores propuseram uma resposta a partir de um experimento de laboratório. Um disco que desce com uma textura girando por dentro é visto descendo na vertical quando olhado de frente. Visto pelo canto do olho, o giro interno parece parar, e o disco parece descer em diagonal, tanto mais inclinado quanto mais periférica a visão. O centro do olho e a periferia processam o movimento de jeitos diferentes. A trajetória da bola começa no centro da visão do rebatedor e, ao se aproximar, passa para a periferia, onde o giro altera a percepção do deslocamento. Os autores aplicaram a ideia também à bola rápida que parece subir. Lançada com giro para trás, ela cai menos do que o esperado, mas nenhum humano consegue arremessá-la rápido o bastante, e com giro suficiente, para que suba de fato.

fontes.trecho: There was once a debate on whether a curveball actually curves or is an optical illusion. In 1949, Ralph B. Lightfoot, an aeronautical engineer at Sikorsky Aircraft, used wind tunnel tests to prove that a curveball curves. [...] However, optical illusion caused by the ball's spinning may play an important part in what makes curveballs difficult to hit. The curveball's trajectory is smooth, but the batter perceives a sudden, dramatic change in the ball's direction. When an object that is spinning and moving through space is viewed directly, the overall motion is interpreted correctly by the brain. However, as it enters the peripheral vision, the internal spinning motion distorts how the overall motion is perceived. A curveball's trajectory begins in the centre of the batter's vision, but overlaps with peripheral vision as it approaches the plate, which may explain the suddenness of the break perceived by the batter. A peer-reviewed article on this hypothesis was published in 2010.

fontes.titulo: Shapiro et al. (2010). Transitions between central and peripheral vision create spatial/temporal distortions: a hypothesis concerning the perceived break of the curveball. PLoS ONE (Europe PMC)
fontes.trecho: The stimulus consists of a descending disk (global motion) with an internal moving grating (local motion). When observers view the disk centrally, they perceive both global and local motion (i.e., observers see the disk's vertical descent and the internal spinning). When observers view the disk peripherally, the internal portion appears stationary, and the disk appears to descend at an angle. The angle of perceived descent increases as the observer views the stimulus from further in the periphery. [...] we present a hypothesis and analysis of the perception of the curveball and rising fastball in the sport of baseball. The curveball is a physically measurable phenomenon: the imbalance of forces created by the ball's spin causes the ball to deviate from a straight line and to follow a smooth parabolic path. However, the curveball is also a perceptual puzzle because batters often report that the flight of the ball undergoes a dramatic and nearly discontinuous shift in position as the ball nears home plate. We suggest that the perception of a discontinuous shift in position results from differences between foveal and peripheral processing.

Fastballs are usually thrown with a backspin so that the Magnus effect creates an upward force on the ball. This causes it to fall less rapidly than expected, and sometimes causes an optical illusion often called a rising fastball. Although it is impossible for a human to throw a baseball fast enough and with enough backspin for the ball to actually rise, to the batter the pitch seems to rise due to the unexpected lack of natural drop on the pitch.

gancho: Nadadores experientes costumam ir mais rápido debaixo d'água do que na superfície. Um costista que chegava a nadar 35 m submerso bateu recordes até 1988, quando as regras passaram a limitar esse trecho: hoje, 15 m.
explicacao: Na superfície a resistência é maior, e por isso, depois da largada e de cada virada, os nadadores costumam ficar submersos até o limite permitido, quase sempre com a pernada de golfinho, que empurra mais que a pernada alternada. O americano David Berkoff levou isso ao extremo no nado de costas. Na Universidade Harvard, passou a fazer largadas e viradas submersas de até 35 metros, com o corpo horizontal, os braços esticados e travados acima da cabeça e uma pernada ondulante. A manobra ganhou o apelido de "Berkoff Blastoff", e em 1988 ele bateu três vezes o recorde mundial dos 100 m costas, sendo o primeiro a nadar a prova em menos de 55 segundos. Ele não estava sozinho: na Olimpíada de 1984, o japonês Daichi Suzuki já tinha nadado 25 metros submerso, e em Seul, em 1988, ficou com o ouro nos 100 m costas, à frente de Berkoff. O longo trecho submerso incomodava os árbitros, e depois dos Jogos de 1988 a FINA o limitou a 10 metros. Entre 1989 e 1991, o limite passou a 15 metros, no costas, no livre e no borboleta. A pernada de golfinho submersa, porém, se espalhou pelas piscinas.

fontes.trecho: Due to increased resistance at the surface, experienced swimmers usually swim faster underwater than at the surface. Therefore, most experienced swimmers in backstroke competitions stay under water up to the limit set by FINA (15 meters after the start and after every turn). Most swimmers use a butterfly kick underwater, as this provides more forward movement than the flutter kick.

He is best known for breaking the world record for the 100-meter backstroke three times, beginning at the 1988 Olympic trial preliminaries, becoming the first swimmer to go under 55 seconds for the event. [...] Known later as the "Berkoff Blastoff", early in his Harvard career, Berkoff began swimming his backstroke start and turns underwater for a distance as long as 35 meters using a powerful push-off from the side of the pool remaining horizontal and as aerodynamic as possible, with a powerful wavelike dolphin kick and outstretched locked arms for the starts and turns. [...] The lengthy underwater start and turn would become controversial with officials, but lead Berkoff to faster times until the rules changed in 1988. [...] but could not match the time in the men's 100-meter backstroke event final where he swam a 55.18, placing him second in the event, and capturing the silver medal. [...] After the 1988 Olympics, a limit of 10 meters was initially set for a few years by FINA officials for the distance a backstroker could swim underwater at their starts and turns, but the use of the underwater dolphin kick at starts and turns with outstretched locked arms would be adopted by a great number of competitive backstroke swimmers as well as butterfly and freestyle swimmers. [...] In 1991, and remaining as of 2022, the distance limit increased to 15 meters at the start and after the turns for backstrokers, butterfly and freestyle swimmers. The limit for backstrokers of 15 meters for backstroke swimmers was set as early as 1989.

However, it was Suzuki who finally developed the skill, allowing him to swim 25 meters underwater at the 1984 Summer Olympics held in Los Angeles. Four years later, he won the gold medal in the 100-meter backstroke at the 1988 Seoul Olympics where Berkoff also competed.

gancho: Num estudo financiado pela Nike, um protótipo de tênis com espuma nova e placa rígida reduziu em 4%, em média, o gasto de energia de 18 corredores de elite, e todos gastaram menos. A espuma era a melhor explicação.
explicacao: No estudo, publicado em 2018 por pesquisadores da Universidade do Colorado, os 18 atletas correram com três calçados: o protótipo e dois tênis de maratona já consagrados, com a massa igualada. Medindo o oxigênio consumido e o gás carbônico produzido, a equipe viu que o protótipo baixou o custo de energia da corrida em cerca de 4%, nas três velocidades testadas, de 14 a 18 km/h. Toda espuma dissipa parte da energia como calor, e a fração que ela devolve se chama resiliência. A areia da praia, por exemplo, é macia mas pouco resiliente, e por isso correr nela cansa mais. Nos testes mecânicos, o protótipo devolveu 7,46 joules por passo, contra 3,38 e 3,56 joules dos outros dois. Placas de carbono sozinhas, segundo trabalhos citados pelos autores, economizam cerca de 1%. O estudo foi pago por um contrato da Nike, e dois coautores eram funcionários da empresa. Os tênis desse tipo chegaram às lojas em 2017 e coincidiram com uma série de recordes: no fim de 2023, 15 dos 20 melhores tempos da maratona eram de 2018 em diante. A World Athletics passou a limitar a altura da sola a 40 mm.

fontes.titulo: Hoogkamer et al. (2018). A Comparison of the Energetic Cost of Running in Marathon Racing Shoes. Sports Medicine (Europe PMC)
fontes.trecho: Recently, prototype running shoes were developed that combine a new highly compliant and resilient midsole material with a stiff embedded plate. [...] 18 high-caliber athletes ran six 5-min trials (three shoes [...] We measured submaximal oxygen uptake and carbon dioxide production during minutes 3 [...] Compared with the established racing shoes, the new shoes reduced the energetic cost of running in all 18 subjects tested. [...] The observed percent changes were independent of running velocity (14 [...] The prototype shoes lowered the energetic cost of running by 4% on average. [...] Inevitably, all foams are viscoelastic; i.e., they dissipate some energy as heat [...] The percent of the stored mechanical energy that is returned is called resilience. Some materials/surfaces are compliant, but have low resilience (e.g., a sandy beach) and thus increase the energetic cost of running [...] Such plates can reduce the energetic cost of running by ~ 1% [...] For now, the elastic properties of the NP shoes provide the best explanation for the metabolic energy savings. Our mechanical testing quantified that the NP shoes returned 7.46 J of mechanical energy per step versus 3.38 and 3.56 J for the NS and AB shoes, respectively [...] This study was supported by a contract from Nike, Inc. with the University of Colorado, Boulder. [...] Emily M. Farina and Geng Luo are employees of Nike, Inc.

These so-called "super shoes" began retailing in 2017. [...] The introduction of super shoes coincided with a series of record-breaking times in long-distance running events. As of late 2023, 15 of the 20 top times for the marathon were set since 2018. [...] World Athletics set guidelines limiting soles of shoes used in competitions to 40 mm (1.6 in) in stack height.

gancho: No meio de um pelotão de ciclistas, a resistência do ar pode cair até 95%. E o vácuo não ajuda só quem vem atrás: em corridas de carros, o da frente também ganha com o que o segue de perto.
explicacao: Quem pedala atrás de outros fica numa zona de pressão menor e gasta menos energia, enquanto quem vai na ponta enfrenta o vento inteiro e se cansa mais. Por isso o pelotão vive em rotação: os da frente recuam para se recuperar e outros assumem o posto. Essa economia molda a tática das provas. Num modelo de computador de uma corrida simulada, os ciclistas mais fracos se deram melhor evitando a frente, enquanto para os mais fortes cooperar valeu a pena. O vácuo tem uma face menos óbvia. Nas pistas ovais mais rápidas da NASCAR, dois ou mais carros enfileirados andam mais rápido do que um sozinho. O de trás aproveita a esteira de baixa pressão deixada pelo primeiro. Ao se aproximar, empurra ar de alta pressão para a frente, e menos ar rápido bate no aerofólio traseiro do líder. Resultado: menos arrasto para os dois. A natureza usa truque parecido. Gansos voam em V porque o redemoinho que se forma na ponta da asa da ave da frente cria uma corrente de ar para cima, que dá sustentação às de trás, e as aves se posicionam perto da distância ideal prevista pela teoria.

fontes.trecho: Riders in a group save energy by riding behind or close to other riders (drafting, or slipstreaming). The reduction in drag is dramatic; riding in the middle of a well-developed group, drag can be reduced by as much as 95%. [...] Riders at the front are fully exposed to wind resistance, hence they experience higher fatigue loads than riders in drafting positions. After a period of time in front, leading riders maneuver farther back in the peloton to a drafting position to recover. [...] Results of the model shows that weaker riders are better off defecting, while cooperation is a good strategy for stronger riders.

drafting can significantly reduce the paceline's average energy expenditure and can even slightly reduce the energy expenditure of the lead vehicle.
