[...] On the faster speedways and superspeedways used by NASCAR and ARCA, two or more vehicles can race faster when lined up front-to-rear than a single car can race alone. The low-pressure wake behind a group's leading car reduces the aerodynamic resistance on the front of the trailing car, allowing the second car to pull closer. As the second car nears the first, it pushes high-pressure air forward so less fast-moving air hits the lead car's spoiler. The result is less drag for both cars, allowing faster speeds. [...] Flocks of geese and some other birds fly in a V formation because the wingtip vortices generated by the front bird will create up-wash circulations. The birds flying behind will receive lift force from these up-wash vortices. [...] Studies show that birds in a V formation place themselves roughly at the optimum distance predicted by simple aerodynamic theory.

gancho: Mergulhadores do povo Sama-Bajau, do Sudeste Asiático, passam mais de 5 horas por dia submersos em apneia. Um estudo de 2018 achou neles baços cerca de 50% maiores que os de um povo vizinho de terra firme.
explicacao: Os Sama-Bajau, povo nômade do mar, vivem há séculos de colher alimento debaixo d'água, e o tempo que seus mergulhadores passam em apneia foi descrito como o maior já registrado em humanos. Mais de mil anos desse modo de vida parecem ter deixado marcas no DNA. Num estudo de 2018, o baço deles era cerca de 50% maior que o dos Saluan, vizinhos que vivem em terra. O tamanho importa porque o baço funciona como uma reserva: quando o mergulhador está no fundo, ele se contrai e despeja no sangue mais hemácias carregadas de hemoglobina, o que permite mergulhos mais longos sem respirar. A diferença parece ligada a uma variante do gene PDE10A. Outros genes com sinais de seleção nesse povo têm a ver com o aperto dos vasos sanguíneos das extremidades, parte do reflexo de mergulho, e com o controle da acidez do sangue quando o gás carbônico se acumula. Segundo os pesquisadores, essas variantes provavelmente ficaram mais comuns por seleção natural. Algo parecido aparece nas haenyeo, mergulhadoras da Coreia do Sul: durante a apneia, o coração delas desacelera de forma acentuada, e elas toleram o frio de modo excepcional, com indícios de variação genética por trás dessas vantagens.

fontes.trecho: Divers work long days with the "greatest daily apnea diving time reported in humans" of greater than 5 hours per day submerged. [...] More than a thousand years of subsistence freediving associated with their life on the sea appear to have endowed the Bajau with several genetic adaptations to facilitate their lifestyle. A 2018 study showed that Bajau spleens are about 50 percent larger than those of a neighbouring land-based group, the Saluan, letting them store more haemoglobin-rich blood, which is expelled into the bloodstream when the spleen contracts at depth, allowing breath-holding dives of longer duration. This difference is apparently related to a variant of the PDE10A gene. Other genes that appear to have been under selection in the Bajau include BDKRB2, which is related to peripheral vasoconstriction, involved in the diving response; FAM178B, a regulator of carbonic anhydrase, which is related to maintaining blood pH when carbon dioxide accumulates; and another one involved in the response to hypoxia. These adaptations were found to likely result from natural selection

Having harvested underwater seafood over centuries, the nomadic Sama-Bajau people of Southeast Asia have enlarged spleens and more intense peripheral vasoconstriction during breath-hold diving [...] Similarly, the Haenyeo women divers of South Korea have pronounced bradycardia and exceptional cold tolerance during breath-hold diving, with evidence of adaptive genetic variation contributing to these advantages.

gancho: Em 1954, o médico John Stapp, nascido em Salvador, freou num trenó-foguete a 1.017 km/h e aguentou 46,2 g. Foi ele quem popularizou a Lei de Murphy, que teria nascido em testes anteriores com trenós.
explicacao: Stapp era filho de missionários batistas e nasceu na Bahia, mas fez carreira como médico da Força Aérea dos Estados Unidos. A pergunta dele era quanta desaceleração um corpo humano suporta num acidente, e ele próprio foi um dos voluntários mais frequentes dos testes. Nos trenós-foguete, quebrou o pulso direito em duas ocasiões, fraturou costelas, perdeu obturações dos dentes e teve sangramentos na retina que o deixaram temporariamente sem enxergar. Na 29.ª e última corrida, em 10 de dezembro de 1954, chegou a 1.017 km/h, acima do recorde de velocidade em terra, e suportou 46,2 g. Descreveu a sensação nos olhos como a de arrancar um molar sem anestesia. Os testes mostraram que um piloto bem preso por cintos pode sair andando de um acidente, desde que o assento não se solte, e que o assento virado para trás é o mais seguro. Anos antes, o engenheiro Edward Murphy propôs medir as forças com sensores presos ao cinto de Stapp; num teste, os sensores falharam porque tinham sido ligados errado, Murphy pôs a culpa no técnico, e a reclamação acabou virando lei. A origem exata é debatida, mas a forma final, "tudo o que pode dar errado vai dar errado", é atribuída a Stapp, que a apresentou numa entrevista coletiva.

fontes.trecho: Born in Salvador de Bahia, Brazil, Stapp was the eldest of four sons of Reverend Charles Franklin Stapp and Mrs. Mary Louise Shannon, Baptist missionaries. [...] Stapp, one of the most frequent volunteers on the runs, sustained a fracture of his right wrist during the runs on two separate occasions, also broke ribs, lost fillings from his teeth and developed bleeding into his retinas that caused temporary vision loss [...] It proved beyond a doubt that this position was the safest for aircraft passengers and required little harness support, and that a human can withstand much greater deceleration than in the forward position. [...] His work showed that a pilot could walk away from crashes when properly protected by harnesses if the seat does not break loose. [...] By riding the decelerator sled, in his 29th and last ride at Holloman Air Force Base in New Mexico, Stapp demonstrated that a human can withstand at least 46.2 g (in the forward position, with adequate harnessing). This is the highest known acceleration voluntarily encountered by a human, set on December 10, 1954. Stapp reached a speed of 632 mph (1,017 km/h), which exceeded the land speed record and made him the fastest man on Earth. Stapp believed that the tolerance of humans to acceleration had not yet been reached in tests. He believed it is much greater than thought possible. He said "I felt a sensation in the eyes, somewhat like the extraction of a molar without anesthetic," [...] Stapp is credited with being the popularizer, as well as the author of the final form of the principle known as Murphy's law, "Anything that can go wrong, will go wrong."

its exact origins are debated, but it is generally agreed it originated from Murphy and his team following a mishap during rocket sled tests some time in 1948 or 1949, and was finalized and first popularized by testing project head John Stapp during a later press conference. gancho: Na virada de 1963 para 1964, o estudante Randy Gardner, de 17 anos, ficou 11 dias sem dormir. Disseram que ele saiu quase ileso, mas quem monitorou sua saúde registrou paranoia, alucinações e falhas de memória.
explicacao: Gardner, de San Diego, ficou 264,4 horas acordado e superou o recorde anterior, de 260 horas. A tentativa teve a presença do pesquisador do sono William Dement, de Stanford, e a saúde do rapaz foi monitorada pelo oficial da Marinha John Ross. Por muito tempo se repetiu que a experiência mostrava que a privação extrema de sono tinha pouco efeito além do mau humor, em boa parte porque Dement contou que, no décimo dia, Gardner o venceu no fliperama. O relato de Ross é outro: mudanças de humor, dificuldade de concentração, problemas de memória recente, paranoia e alucinações. No décimo primeiro dia, pediram que ele subtraísse sete seguidamente a partir de 100; parou no 65 e explicou que tinha esquecido o que estava fazendo. Depois, dormiu 14 horas e 46 minutos, e exames semanas mais tarde não mostraram diferenças importantes. Em 2017, porém, ele disse ter insônia séria desde por volta de 2007 e culpou a experiência. Recordes assim são difíceis de conferir, porque a pessoa pode ter microcochilos sem perceber. Desde 1997, o Guinness não aceita novas tentativas, por segurança.

fontes.trecho: Randy Gardner (born 1946) is an American man from San Diego, California, who once held the record for the longest amount of time a human has gone without sleep. Between December 1963 and January 1964, the then 17-year-old Gardner stayed awake for 11 days and 25 minutes (264.4 hours), breaking the previous record of 260 hours held by Tom Rounds. Gardner's record was then broken repeatedly until 1997, when Guinness World Records ceased accepting new attempts for safety reasons. [...] Gardner's record attempt was attended by Stanford sleep researcher Dr. William C. Dement, while his health was monitored by Lt. Cmdr. John J. Ross. [...] It has been claimed that Gardner's experiment demonstrated that extreme sleep deprivation has little effect, other than the mood changes associated with tiredness, primarily due to a report by researcher William C. Dement, who stated that on the tenth day of the experiment, Gardner had been, among other things, able to beat Dement at pinball. However, contrary to this, Lieutenant Commander John J. Ross, who monitored his health, reported serious cognitive and behavioral changes. These included moodiness, problems with concentration and short-term memory, paranoia, and hallucinations. On the eleventh day, when he was asked to subtract seven repeatedly, starting with 100, he stopped at 65. When asked why he had stopped, he replied that he had forgotten what he was doing. [...] After completing his record, Gardner slept for 14 hours and 46 minutes [...] with follow-up sleep recordings taken one, six, and ten weeks after the fact, showing no significant differences. However, in 2017, Gardner reported that he started experiencing serious insomnia around 2007, decades after his sleep experiment, and believed his participation in the 1960s sleep study was to blame. [...] It is difficult to determine the accuracy of a sleep deprivation period unless the participant is carefully observed to detect short microsleeps, which the participant might not even notice.

gancho: Em 1965, um escocês de 207 kg começou um jejum acompanhado por médicos que durou 382 dias, à base de chá, café, água com gás e vitaminas. Terminou com 82 kg, e a primeira refeição foi um ovo cozido.
explicacao: Angus Barbieri tinha 27 anos quando se internou num hospital de Dundee, na Escócia. Os médicos planejavam um jejum curto, porque consideravam os curtos preferíveis aos longos, mas ele insistiu em continuar: estava se adaptando bem e queria chegar ao peso que considerava ideal. Começou no hospital, mas passou a maior parte do tempo em casa, voltando para exames de sangue e de urina. Nesse período, consumiu apenas vitaminas, eletrólitos, um pouco de levedura e bebidas sem calorias, às vezes com leite ou açúcar, sobretudo nas últimas semanas. Com o tempo, perdeu toda a vontade de comer, e há relatos de que chegou a ficar 48 dias sem evacuar. O jejum terminou em 30 de junho de 1966; depois de dez dias de transição, com sal e depois açúcar, em 11 de julho ele comeu um ovo cozido e uma fatia de pão com manteiga e disse aos repórteres que tinha esquecido o gosto da comida. Perdeu 125 kg. Um estudo de 1973 encontrou-o com 89 kg e concluiu que, nesse paciente, o jejum prolongado não deixara efeitos nocivos. O Guinness reconheceu o recorde na edição de 1971, mas hoje não incentiva recordes de jejum, por medo de estimular comportamentos perigosos. É um caso isolado, feito com acompanhamento médico e suplementos, e não uma prova de que jejuns longos sejam seguros.

fontes.trecho: was a Scottish man who fasted for 382 days, from 14 June 1965 to 30 June 1966. He subsisted on tea, coffee, sparkling water, vitamins and yeast extract while living at home in Tayport, Scotland, frequently visiting Maryfield Hospital for medical evaluation. Barbieri went from almost 33 stone / 456 pounds (207 kg) to 13 stone / 180 pounds (82 kg), losing 20 stone / 276 pounds (125 kg) and setting a record for the length of a fast. [...] In 1965, at the age of 27, Barbieri checked into the Maryfield Hospital in Dundee. Initially only a short fast was planned; doctors believed short fasts were preferable to longer ones. Barbieri insisted on continuing because "he adapted so well and was eager to reach his 'ideal' weight". [...] As the fast progressed, he lost all desire for food. For 382 days, from 14 June 1965 through 30 June 1966, he consumed only vitamins, electrolytes, an unspecified amount of yeast (a source of all essential amino acids) and zero-calorie beverages such as tea, coffee, and sparkling water, although he occasionally added milk and/or sugar to the beverages, especially during the final weeks of the fast. Barbieri began his treatment in the hospital but for most of the 382 days lived at home, visiting the hospital for outpatient checkups, including blood and urine samples. Stool tests were not taken but he reportedly went up to 48 days between stools. [...] Angus Barbieri ate his first solid meal at 10 AM on 11 July 1966: a boiled egg and a slice of buttered bread. He said to the gathered newspaper reporters and photographers, "I have forgotten what food tasted like [...] In the 1971 edition of The Guinness Book of Records, Barbieri's 382-day fast was recognized as the longest recorded. [...] Guinness does not actively encourage records relating to fasting for fear of encouraging unsafe behaviour. [...] a 1973 study found that Barbieri maintained a healthy weight of 14 stone / 196 pounds (89 kg), concluding that "prolonged fasting in this patient had no ill-effects". [...] For the next ten days, the doctors placed him on a diet of salt and then sugar in preparation for solid food.

gancho: Em 1999, uma médica sueca ficou 80 minutos presa sob o gelo na Noruega. Chegou ao hospital com o corpo a 13,7 °C, passou 2 h 35 min sem batimentos e se recuperou quase por completo.
explicacao: Anna Bågenholm, então com 29 anos, esquiava perto de Narvik quando caiu de cabeça num riacho congelado. Ficou presa sob uma camada de gelo de 20 centímetros, com só os pés e os esquis para fora. Achou um bolsão de ar e se manteve consciente por 40 minutos, até a circulação parar. Os colegas, também médicos, fizeram massagem cardíaca assim que ela foi retirada, e a reanimação continuou no helicóptero até o hospital de Tromsø. Lá, o eletrocardiograma não mostrava sinal de vida, mas o chefe da emergência seguiu a regra de aquecer o paciente antes de declarar a morte. Uma máquina de circulação extracorpórea aqueceu o sangue fora do corpo, e o coração voltou a bater às 22h15. Mais de cem médicos e enfermeiros se revezaram por nove horas. Ela acordou dez dias depois, paralisada do pescoço para baixo, e se recuperou quase totalmente, restando sintomas leves nas mãos e nos pés. O segredo, segundo o médico, é que o corpo esfriou por inteiro antes de o coração parar: com o cérebro tão frio, os neurônios precisavam de pouquíssimo oxigênio. Abaixo de 28 °C, sobrevivem só de 10% a 33% dos adultos. O recorde anterior, 14,4 °C, era de uma criança.

fontes.trecho: who survived after a skiing accident in 1999 left her trapped under a layer of ice for 80 minutes in freezing water. [...] After rescue, Bågenholm was transported by helicopter to the Tromsø University Hospital, where a team of more than a hundred doctors and nurses worked in shifts for nine hours to save her life. Bågenholm woke up ten days after the accident, paralyzed from the neck down [...] Although she has made an almost full recovery from the incident, late in 2009 she was still having minor symptoms in hands and feet related to nerve injury. [...] At the time of the incident, she was 29 years old [...] On that day, Bågenholm was skiing in the mountains outside of Narvik [...] She fell headfirst onto a layer of ice on a frozen stream near a waterfall, landing on her back. [...] Her body became trapped under the ice, which was 20 centimetres (7.9 in) thick. When Falkenberg and Næsheim found Bågenholm, only her feet and skis were above the ice. [...] she found an air pocket and was able to remain conscious for 40 minutes before experiencing circulatory arrest. [...] Falkenberg and Næsheim, both doctors, began giving her cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR). [...] The helicopter emergency team continued to give her CPR during the flight [...] Her body temperature at this point was 13.7 °C (56.7 °F), the lowest survived body temperature ever recorded in a human with accidental hypothermia at the time. Dr. Mads Gilbert, an anesthesiologist and the chief of the hospital's emergency room, proceeded with the resuscitation attempt. [...] The electrocardiogram connected to her showed no signs of life, but Gilbert knew patients should be "warmed up before you declare them dead". [...] she was connected to a cardiopulmonary bypass machine that warmed up her blood outside of her body before it was reinserted into her veins. Bågenholm's first heart beat was recorded at 22:15 [...] She had no heart beat for 2 hours 35 minutes, from 19:40 till 22:15. [...] The survival rate for adults whose body temperature has decreased to below 28 °C (82 °F) is 10%–33%. Prior to Bågenholm's accident, the lowest survived body temperature was 14.4 °C (57.9 °F), which had been recorded in a child. [...] "Her body had time to cool down completely before the heart stopped. Her brain was so cold when the heart stopped that the brain cells needed very little oxygen, so the brain could survive for quite a prolonged time."

gancho: Uma das ultramaratonas mais duras do mundo nasceu de uma piada: o assassino de Martin Luther King fugiu da prisão e andou só 13 km em 54 horas. O criador da prova pensou que faria pelo menos 160 km.
explicacao: Em 1977, James Earl Ray, condenado pelo assassinato de Luther King, fugiu da penitenciária de Brushy Mountain, no Tennessee, e percorreu cerca de 13 km nas 54 horas seguintes. Debochando da marca, Gary Cantrell, que usa o apelido Lazarus Lake, decidiu que faria pelo menos 100 milhas, cerca de 160 km, na mata vizinha. Assim nasceu a Barkley Marathons, corrida pela primeira vez em 1986 e batizada com o nome de um vizinho dele. No formato atual, são cinco voltas sem marcação, oficialmente de 32 km cada, mas estimadas em cerca de 40 km, com limite de 60 horas e água em só dois pontos. Para provar que passaram por todo o percurso, os corredores precisam achar de 9 a 15 livros escondidos e arrancar de cada um a página com o número do seu peito. A inscrição custa 1,60 dólar, inclui perguntas absurdas e uma redação, e a largada é dada quando Cantrell acende um cigarro. Depois que a prisão fechou, em 2009, o trajeto passou a incluir um túnel sob ela. Até o fim da edição de 2026, a prova completa tinha sido terminada dentro do prazo só 26 vezes, por 20 pessoas. Em 2024, a britânica Jasmin Paris foi a primeira mulher a conseguir, 99 segundos antes do limite.

fontes.trecho: The Barkley Marathons is an ultramarathon trail race held each year in Frozen Head State Park in Morgan County, Tennessee, United States. [...] The course, which varies from year to year, consists of five loops of 20 miles (32 km) of off-trail course for a total of 100 miles (160 km) of harsh terrain. The race is limited to a 60-hour period from the start of the first loop [...] The idea for the race was inspired by the 1977 escape of James Earl Ray, who was convicted for the assassination of Martin Luther King Jr., from nearby Brushy Mountain State Penitentiary. Ray covered only about 8 miles (13 km) after escaping for 54 hours. Mocking Ray's low mileage, Cantrell said to himself, "I could do at least 100 miles". Thus, the Barkley Marathons were born. Cantrell named the race for his longtime neighbor and running companion, Barry Barkley. [...] The race was first run in 1986. [...] In 2009, Brushy Mountain State Penitentiary closed, allowing it to eventually become part of the Barkley course including a tunnel under the prison and a pass by the wall through which Ray escaped. [...] In 2024, Paris became the first woman to complete all five loops within the time limit, finishing the event 99 seconds before the 60-hour cut-off. [...] and pay a $1.60 application fee, representing one penny per mile for both the 60-mile and 100-mile races. Additionally, an entry form must also be completed which includes bizarre and irrelevant questions. [...] This is followed by a written essay on "Why I Should be Allowed to Run in the Barkley." [...] It currently consists of an unmarked loop [...] the current estimate being around 25 miles (40 km) per loop while "officially" the loop is still stated to be 20 miles (32 km). [...] There are no aid stations, except water in two places. [...] the race officially begins when Cantrell lights a cigarette. In addition to running, competitors must find between 9 and 15 books along the course (the exact number varies each year) and remove the page corresponding to the runner's race number from each book as proof of completion. [...] As of the end of the 2026 event, the full, five-loop race has been completed within 60 hours a total of 26 times by 20 runners.

gancho: O Guinness lista a comissária Vesna Vulović como sobrevivente da queda mais alta sem paraquedas: 10.160 m, em 1972. Em 2009, jornalistas disseram que o avião foi abatido a 800 m; as autoridades tchecas rejeitaram a tese.
explicacao: Em 26 de janeiro de 1972, uma explosão no compartimento de bagagens partiu um DC-9 da companhia iugoslava JAT sobre a então Tchecoslováquia. Os investigadores atribuíram a explosão a uma bomba numa maleta. Das 28 pessoas a bordo, só Vesna sobreviveu. Segundo os investigadores, ela ficou presa por um carrinho de comida dentro de um pedaço da fuselagem, que caiu inclinado numa encosta coberta de mata e de neve, o que amorteceu o impacto. Fraturou o crânio, três vértebras, as pernas, a pelve e costelas, passou dias em coma e ficou temporariamente paralisada da cintura para baixo, mas voltou a andar em dez meses. Não guardou memória da queda. Os médicos dela atribuíram parte da sorte à pressão baixa, que a teria feito desmaiar logo após a despressurização; ela contou que, sabendo disso, tinha tomado muito café antes do exame médico da empresa para ser aprovada. Em 1985, o Guinness reconheceu o recorde. Em 2009, dois jornalistas de Praga disseram que o avião fora abatido por engano pela força aérea tchecoslovaca, a 800 m, e que o recorde seria uma farsa da polícia secreta. A autoridade de aviação tcheca chamou a ideia de teoria da conspiração, e um dos jornalistas admitiu que as provas eram circunstanciais. O Guinness mantém o recorde.

fontes.trecho: 3 January 1950 – 23 December 2016) was a Serbian flight attendant who survived the highest fall without a parachute: 10,160 metres (33,330 feet; 6.31 miles). She was the sole survivor of JAT Flight 367 after an explosion tore through the baggage compartment on 26 January 1972 [...] Air safety investigators attributed the explosion to a briefcase bomb. [...] Following the bombing, Vulović spent days in a coma and was hospitalized for several months. She suffered a fractured skull, three broken vertebrae, broken legs, broken ribs, and a fractured pelvis. These injuries resulted in her being temporarily paralyzed from the waist down. [...] She had little to no memory of the incident [...] The aircraft, a McDonnell Douglas DC-9 [...] Vulović was the only survivor of the 28 passengers and crew. [...] Air safety investigators attributed Vulović's survival to her being trapped by a food trolley in the DC-9's fuselage as it broke away from the rest of the aircraft and plummeted towards the ground. [...] Investigators believed that the fuselage, with Vulović pinned inside, landed at an angle in a heavily wooded and snow-covered mountainside, which cushioned the impact. Vulović's physicians concluded that her history of low blood pressure caused her to pass out quickly after the cabin depressurized [...] Vulović said that she was aware of her low blood pressure before applying to become a flight attendant and knew that it would result in her failing her medical examination, but she drank an excessive amount of coffee beforehand and was accepted. [...] Within ten months, Vulović had regained the ability to walk [...] In 1985, The Guinness Book of World Records recognized Vulović as the world record holder for surviving the highest fall without a parachute [...] In 2009, Peter Hornung and Pavel Theiner, two Prague-based journalists, claimed that Flight 367 had been mistaken for an enemy aircraft and shot down by the Czechoslovak Air Force at an altitude of 800 metres (2,600 ft), far lower than the official altitude of 10,160 metres (33,330 ft). The two claimed that the Czechoslovak State Security had conjured up Vulović's record fall as part of a cover-up. [...] The Czech Civil Aviation Authority dismissed the journalists' claim, calling it a conspiracy theory. Hornung conceded that the pair's evidence was only circumstantial. [...] Guinness World Records continues to list her as the record-holder for surviving the highest fall without a parachute.

gancho: Na véspera do Natal de 1971, um raio atingiu um avião sobre a Amazônia peruana. Juliane Koepcke caiu cerca de 3 km presa à poltrona, sobreviveu e passou mais de uma semana sozinha na selva até achar ajuda.
explicacao: Juliane era filha de dois zoólogos alemães que viviam no Peru. Aos 14 anos, foi com eles montar a estação de pesquisa Panguana, na floresta, onde aprendeu a sobreviver na mata. Em 24 de dezembro de 1971, um dia depois da formatura no colégio, embarcou com a mãe num voo da LANSA. O avião foi atingido por um raio, se desfez no ar, e ela caiu ainda presa à fileira de poltronas. Especialistas acham que o conjunto de três assentos pode ter funcionado como um paraquedas, e que a corrente de ar da tempestade e a mata fechada podem ter amortecido a queda. Com a clavícula quebrada, um corte no braço e um ligamento do joelho rompido, seguiu um riacho até um rio. Larvas de mosca se instalaram no ferimento. Depois de nove dias, achou um acampamento de madeireiros, que despejaram gasolina no corte e a levaram de canoa por 11 horas. Até 14 outros passageiros sobreviveram à queda, mas morreram à espera de resgate. Juliane virou bióloga especialista em morcegos e, em 2000, assumiu a direção da Panguana. O cineasta Werner Herzog, que só não estava no mesmo voo por uma mudança de planos de última hora, contou a história dela no documentário Wings of Hope ("Asas da esperança"), de 1998.

fontes.trecho: is a German-Peruvian mammalogist who specialises in bats. She is the daughter of German zoologists Maria and Hans-Wilhelm Koepcke. [...] When the plane was struck by lightning, she fell 3,000 m (10,000 ft) while strapped to her seat [...] At the age of 14, she left Lima with her parents to establish the Panguana research station in the Amazon rainforest, where she learned survival skills. [...] graduating on 23 December 1971. [...] On 24 December 1971, just one day after she graduated, Koepcke flew on LANSA Flight 508. [...] The plane was struck by lightning mid-flight and began to disintegrate before plummeting to the ground. Koepcke found herself falling, still strapped to her row of seats, [...] Koepcke survived the fall but suffered injuries including a broken collarbone, a deep cut on her right arm, an eye injury, a ruptured ligament in her knee, and a concussion. She then spent 11 days in the rainforest, most of which she spent following a creek to a river. While in the jungle, she dealt with severe insect bites and an infestation of botfly larvae in her injured arm. After nine days, she was able to find an encampment that had been set up by local lumberjacks. A few hours later, the returning lumberjacks found her, poured gasoline onto her wound, and used a canoe to transport her for 11 hours to a more inhabited area. [...] Experts have said that she survived the fall because she was harnessed into her seat, the window seat, which was attached to the two seats to her left as part of a row of three. That was thought to have functioned as a parachute or helicopter which slowed her fall. The impact may have also been lessened by the updraft from a thunderstorm Koepcke fell through, as well as the thick foliage at her landing site. As many as 14 other passengers were later discovered to have survived the initial crash but died while waiting to be rescued. [...] In 2000, following the death of her father, she took over as the director of Panguana. [...] Koepcke's story was more faithfully told by Koepcke herself in German filmmaker Werner Herzog's documentary Wings of Hope (1998). Herzog was interested in telling her story because of a personal connection: He was scheduled to be on the same flight while scouting locations for his film Aguirre, the Wrath of God (1972), but a last-minute change of plans spared him from the crash.

gancho: Jeanne Calment morreu em 1997 aos 122 anos, mais de três anos além de qualquer outra pessoa documentada. Uma tese diz que a filha assumiu o lugar dela; a maioria dos especialistas a rejeita, e um exame de DNA resolveria.
explicacao: Nascida em Arles, na França, em 1875, Calment é a única pessoa com idade verificada a chegar aos 120 anos. Também é das mais bem documentadas: aparece em 14 recenseamentos, o primeiro de 1876, quando tinha um ano. Fumou até os 117 e contava ter conhecido Van Gogh aos 13 ou 14 anos, na loja de tecidos de um tio, que ele seria desagradável e cheiraria a álcool. Para os demógrafos, a idade dela é um ponto fora da curva: entre os recordistas, as diferenças costumam ser de meses ou semanas. Em 2018, o gerontólogo russo Valery Novoselov e o matemático Nikolay Zak retomaram a hipótese de que Jeanne teria morrido em 1934 e a filha, Yvonne, nascida em 1898, teria assumido a identidade da mãe, morrendo portanto aos 99. A maioria dos especialistas considera a tese fraca. O demógrafo Jean-Marie Robine lembrou que Calment respondeu corretamente a perguntas sobre fatos que a filha não teria como conhecer de primeira mão, e cientistas franceses publicaram em 2019 uma refutação. A dúvida, porém, tem solução simples: como Jeanne se casou com um primo de segundo grau duplo, Yvonne tinha só 12 trisavós distintos, contra 16 da mãe. Um tipo específico de exame de DNA resolveria a questão, se houvesse uma amostra de sangue ou tecido disponível.

fontes.trecho: 21 February 1875 – 4 August 1997) was a French supercentenarian who is the oldest person in recorded history whose age has been verified, with a documented lifespan of 122 years and 164 days. [...] Calment is the only person in history who has been verified to have reached the age of 120 years. [...] Calment claimed to reporters that she had met van Gogh at that time, introduced to him by her future husband in her uncle's fabric shop. [...] She described his personality as ugly, ungracious, and "very disagreeable", adding that he "reeked of alcohol". [...] when she was 13 and 14 years old. [...] Calment is widely regarded as the best-documented supercentenarian recorded. For example, she was listed in fourteen census records, beginning in 1876 as a one-year-old infant. [...] Demographers have highlighted that Calment's age is an outlier, her lifespan being more than three years longer than the next oldest people ever documented, where the differences are usually by months or weeks. [...] In 2018, Russian gerontologist Valery Novoselov and mathematician Nikolay Zak revived the hypothesis that Jeanne died in 1934 and her daughter Yvonne, born in 1898, assumed her mother's official identity and was therefore 99 years old when she died in 1997. [...] This hypothesis is considered weak by mainstream longevity experts, such as French gerontologist Jean-Marie Robine, who pointed out that during his research, Calment had correctly answered questions about things that her daughter could not have known first-hand. [...] that Novoselov and Zak's claims have been dismissed by the overwhelming majority of experts [...] In September 2019, several French scientists released a paper in The Journals of Gerontology pointing out inaccuracies in the Zak et al. paper. [...] Since Jeanne Calment had 16 distinct great-great-grandparents while her daughter Yvonne had only 12, geneticists have noted that the question of identity could easily be settled by a test for autozygous DNA if a blood or tissue sample were to be made available. [...] Calment continued smoking in her elderly years until she was 117. [...] Jeanne married her double second cousin, Fernand Nicolas Calment (1868–1942). Their paternal grandfathers were brothers, and their paternal grandmothers were sisters.

gancho: Desde 1980, uma corrida no País de Gales põe gente a pé contra cavalos montados em cerca de 35 km de serra. Um corredor venceu pela primeira vez em 2004. Uma hipótese debatida diz que evoluímos para correr longe.
explicacao: A prova nasceu num pub de Llanwrtyd Wells: o dono, Gordon Green, ouviu dois fregueses discutindo se, numa distância longa e em terreno variado, um homem se igualaria a um cavalo, e resolveu testar em público. Em 1989, um ciclista venceu o primeiro cavalo, mas só em 2004 um corredor a pé, Huw Lobb, ganhou a corrida, em 2 horas, 5 minutos e 19 segundos, levando um prêmio de 25 mil libras que crescia mil libras a cada ano sem vencedor humano. Em 2007, os corredores repetiram o feito, quase 11 minutos à frente do primeiro cavalo. A hipótese da corrida de resistência propõe que o corpo do gênero Homo foi moldado para correr longas distâncias: nenhum outro primata faz isso, e temos tendão de Aquiles que funciona como mola, glúteos grandes e um sistema eficiente de suor para perder calor. Assim, nossos ancestrais poderiam perseguir presas até a exaustão em dias quentes, quando quadrúpedes grandes têm dificuldade de se resfriar. Há críticas fortes: vários desses traços já existiam em australopitecos ou parecem ter evoluído para caminhar, com a corrida como subproduto, e a atividade dos glúteos indica que eles servem mais a movimentos rápidos e potentes.

fontes.trecho: The Man versus Horse Marathon is an annual race over 21 miles (34 km), where runners compete against riders on horseback through a mix of road, trail and mountainous terrain. [...] The event started in 1980, when local landlord Gordon Green overheard a discussion between two men in his pub, the Neuadd Arms. One man suggested that over a significant distance across country, man was equal to any horse. Green decided that the challenge should be tested in full public view, and organised the first event. [...] takes place in the Welsh town of Llanwrtyd Wells every June. [...] The course is slightly shorter than a traditional marathon at a reported 22 miles (35 km), but over rougher terrain. [...] In 1989, British cyclist Tim Gould beat the first horse by three minutes – the first time that a horse was beaten by a human in the race. [...] In 2004, the 25th race was won by Huw Lobb in 2 hours, 5 minutes and 19 seconds. It was the first time that a man racing on foot had won the race, thereby winning the prize fund of £25,000, which had been growing by £1,000 each year from the race's inception until claimed by a winning runner. [...] The feat was repeated in 2007, when human competitors outpaced the first equine competitor by almost 11 minutes.

The endurance running hypothesis is a series of conjectures which presume humans evolved anatomical and physiological adaptations to run long distances [...] No primates other than humans are capable of endurance running, and in fact, Australopithecus did not have structural adaptations for running. Instead, forensic anthropology suggests that anatomical features that directly contributed to endurance running capabilities were heavily selected for within the genus Homo dating back to 1.9Ma. [...] This tactic of exhausting prey was especially advantageous for capturing large quadrupedal mammals struggling to thermoregulate in hot weather and over extended distances. Conversely, humans possess efficient means to dissipate heat, primarily through sweating. [...] large gluteal muscles are crucial for erect bipedal locomotion [...] Achilles tendon springs conserve energy [...] From a study of those reports, hindlimb proposed traits were already present in Australopithecus or early Homo. Those hindlimb characteristics most likely evolved to improve walking efficiency with improved running as a by-product. [...] The data suggests that the large size of the gluteus maximus reflects multiple roles during rapid and powerful movements rather than a specific adaptation to submaximal endurance running.

gancho: E se a exaustão numa prova longa não for pane do músculo, mas um freio do cérebro? Pela hipótese do "governador central", ainda debatida, a fadiga é uma sensação criada para proteger o corpo.
explicacao: A ideia tem mais de um século. Em 1924, Archibald Hill, Nobel de Medicina de 1922, sugeriu que algum mecanismo no corpo funcionaria como um "governador", protegendo o coração da falta de oxigênio no esforço intenso. A proposta foi deixada de lado, e a fadiga passou a ser explicada como falha mecânica do próprio músculo: falta de oxigênio, acúmulo de ácido lático ou esgotamento de energia. Em 1997, o cientista do esporte Tim Noakes, da Universidade da Cidade do Cabo, retomou o argumento, e a teoria completa saiu em 2004 e 2005. Por ela, o cérebro ajusta o tempo todo quantas fibras musculares recruta, com base em experiências anteriores, na duração planejada do esforço e no estado do corpo naquele momento, guardando sempre uma reserva de emergência. Esse controle fica fora da consciência e é sentido como cansaço. A favor, há o efeito forte de placebos não só em provas longas, mas até na velocidade de corrida curta e no peso máximo levantado. Contra, há colapsos reais de maratonistas, que sugerem que esse freio pode ser vencido, e fatores do próprio músculo que também protegem contra a catástrofe. A disputa continua aberta.

fontes.trecho: The central governor is a proposed process in the brain that regulates exercise in regard to a neurally calculated safe  exertion by the body. [...] The central governor limits exercise by reducing the neural recruitment of muscle fibers. This reduced recruitment causes the sensation of fatigue. [...] The existence of a central governor was proposed by Tim Noakes in 1997, but a similar idea was suggested in 1924 by Archibald Hill. It was first published as a full theory by Tim Noakes, Alan St Clair Gibson and Vicki Lambert in five linked articles in the British Journal of Sports Medicine in 2004-2005 [...] The 1922 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine winner Archibald Hill proposed in 1924 that the heart was protected from anoxia in strenuous exercise by the existence of a governor. [...] This hypothesis was disregarded and further research upon exercise fatigue was modeled in terms of it being due to a mechanical failure of the exercising muscles ("peripheral muscle fatigue"). This failure was caused either by an inadequate oxygen supply to the exercising muscles, lactic acid buildup, or total energy depletion in the exhausted muscles. [...] Tim Noakes, a professor of exercise and sports science at the University of Cape Town, in 1997 has renewed Hill's argument on the basis of modern research. [...] These neural calculations factor in earlier experience with strenuous exercise, the planning duration of the exercise, and the present metabolic state of the body. These brain models ensure that body homeostasis is protected, and an emergency reserve margin is maintained. This neural control adjusts the number of activated skeletal muscle motor units, a control which is subjectively experienced as fatigue. This process, though occurring in the brain, is outside conscious control. [...] placebos (which must be mediated by a central process) have a powerful effect upon not only fatigue in prolonged exercise, but also upon short term endurance exercise such as sprint speed, the maximum weight that could be lifted with leg extension [...] The existence of a central governor over physiology has been questioned since 'physiological catastrophes' can and do occur in athletes (important examples in marathons have been Dorando Pietri, Jim Peters and Gabriela Andersen-Schiess). This suggests that humans can over-ride 'the central governor'. Moreover, a variety of peripheral factors in addition to those such as lactic acid build up can impair muscle power and might act to protect against "catastrophe".

gancho: No topo do Everest, o oxigênio do ar tem só cerca de um terço da pressão do nível do mar. Até 1978, havia quem duvidasse que alguém subisse lá sem cilindro. Messner e Habeler subiram.
explicacao: A proporção de oxigênio no ar, de 20,9%, é a mesma no alto da montanha. O que cai com a altitude é a pressão do ar e, com ela, a pressão parcial do oxigênio. Acima de 8.000 metros fica a chamada zona da morte, conceito criado em 1953 pelo médico suíço Edouard Wyss-Dunant, que a chamou de zona letal. Ali, acredita-se que nenhum corpo humano consegue se aclimatar: ele gasta o oxigênio mais depressa do que consegue repor, e uma permanência longa sem cilindro leva à deterioração das funções do corpo e à morte. Já acima de 7.500 metros, dormir fica muito difícil e digerir comida, quase impossível. O limite para morar parece estar perto dos 5.950 metros, altitude em que há registro de pessoas que sobreviveram por dois anos. Em 8 de maio de 1978, o italiano Reinhold Messner e o austríaco Peter Habeler chegaram ao cume sem oxigênio suplementar, algo que certos médicos e montanhistas consideravam impossível. Em 1980, Messner repetiu a subida sozinho, sem oxigênio e sem equipe de apoio, e depois se tornou o primeiro a escalar as 14 montanhas de mais de 8.000 metros, todas sem cilindro.

fontes.trecho: This point is generally considered to be 8,000 m (26,246.72 ft), where atmospheric pressure is less than 356 millibars [...] The concept was conceived in 1953 by Edouard Wyss-Dunant, a Swiss doctor, who called it the lethal zone. [...] An extended stay above 8,000 m (26,200 ft) without a high-altitude breathing apparatus (which includes bottled oxygen) will result in deterioration of bodily functions and death. [...] The concentration of oxygen (O2) in air is 20.9% [...] Atmospheric pressure decreases with altitude while the O2 fraction remains constant to about 85 km (53 mi), so PO2 decreases with altitude as well. [...] Humans have survived for 2 years at 5,950 m (19,500 ft) [475 millibars (14.0 inHg; 6.89 psi) of atmospheric pressure], which appears to be near the limit of the permanently tolerable highest altitude. At extreme altitudes, above 7,500 m (24,600 ft) [383 millibars (11.3 inHg; 5.55 psi) of atmospheric pressure], sleeping becomes very difficult, digesting food is near-impossible [...] In the death zone and higher, no human body can acclimatize. The body uses up its store of oxygen faster than it can be replenished.

fontes.titulo: Effects of high altitude on humans
fontes.trecho: It is about half of its sea-level value at 5,000 m (16,000 ft), the altitude of the Everest Base Camp, and only a third at 8,848 m (29,029 ft), the summit of Mount Everest. [...] mountaineers refer to the altitudes above 8,000 metres (26,000 ft) as the death zone, where it is generally believed that no human body can acclimatize.

is an Italian climber, explorer, and author from the German-speaking province of South Tyrol. [...] He was the first person to climb all 14 eight-thousanders, doing so without supplementary oxygen. [...] In 1978, he reached the summit of Everest with Habeler. This was the first time anyone had been that high without supplemental oxygen and Messner and Habeler achieved what certain doctors, specialists, and mountaineers thought impossible. [...] On 8 May 1978, Messner and Habeler reached the summit of Mount Everest, becoming the first men to climb it without using supplemental oxygen. Before this ascent, it was disputed whether this was possible at all. [...] Two years later, on 20 August 1980, Messner again stood atop the highest mountain in the world, without supplementary oxygen. [...] Author Jon Krakauer calls Messner's 1980 ascent of Everest alone, without relying on oxygen, established camps, fixed ropes, or a support team, "still the greatest mountaineering feat of all time".
Peter Habeler (born 22 July 1942) is an Austrian mountaineer.

gancho: Em 1979, um jovem austríaco foi posto numa cela de porão e esquecido: cada um dos três policiais achou que outro o tinha soltado. Sobreviveu 18 dias sem comida, só com a água que se condensava nas paredes.
explicacao: Andreas Mihavecz, de Bregenz, tinha 18 anos e estava de passageiro num carro que bateu. Em 1.º de abril de 1979, foi levado por engano para uma cela de custódia. Os três policiais responsáveis por ele o esqueceram, cada um certo de que os outros dois já o tinham libertado, e ignoraram os apelos da mãe, preocupada com o sumiço do filho. Como a cela ficava no porão, ninguém ouvia os gritos. Ele sobreviveu ingerindo a água condensada nas paredes e perdeu 24 kg. Dezoito dias depois, um policial que foi ao porão por outro motivo sentiu o mau cheiro e abriu a cela. Mihavecz levou semanas para se recuperar. No processo criminal, os três policiais acusaram uns aos outros e só pagaram multa, porque não houve prova de negligência criminosa nem de quem era o principal culpado. Dois anos depois, a Justiça civil lhe deu uma indenização. O caso está no Guinness como o de mais tempo sobrevivido sem comida nem líquidos, e entrou num livro alemão de lendas urbanas como versão moderna de um conto medieval: o do camponês esquecido na prisão de devedores.

fontes.trecho: is an Austrian man from Bregenz who holds the record of surviving the longest without any food or liquids. His ordeal is documented in the Guinness World Records. [...] On 1 April 1979, the then 18-year-old Mihavecz was mistakenly put into custody in a holding cell for being a passenger in a crashed car and completely forgotten about by the three policemen responsible for him. Each of them thought that the two others had already freed Mihavecz. They also ignored the pleas of his worried mother, who was concerned for what might have happened to her son. As Mihavecz's cell was in the basement, nobody could hear his screams. He survived by ingesting condensed water from the walls and eventually lost 24 kg (53 pounds) of weight. Eighteen days later on 19 April, an officer who had unrelated business in the basement opened his cell after noticing the stench that was emanating from it. Mihavecz needed several weeks to regain his health. [...] In the criminal trial that followed, the three policemen accused each other. In the end, they were fined 4000 ATS, an amount equivalent to €990 or AU$1500 in 2026, as there was no evidence of criminal neglect or who was the main culprit. Two years later, however, a civil court awarded Mihavecz 250,000 ATS [...] Mihavecz's case was later included in the first edition of a German book on urban legends, as the updated form of a medieval German folk tale of the forgotten peasant in the debtors' prison.

gancho: As regras do Jogo Real de Ur, da antiga Mesopotâmia, foram reconstruídas a partir de uma tabuinha babilônica de c. 177 a.C. E uma versão dele resistiu entre judeus de Kochi, na Índia, até os anos 1950.
explicacao: O jogo ganhou esse nome porque os primeiros tabuleiros foram achados pelo arqueólogo Leonard Woolley no Cemitério Real de Ur, escavado entre 1922 e 1934. Um deles, hoje no Museu Britânico, é datado de cerca de 2600 a 2400 a.C., o que o põe entre os tabuleiros mais antigos do mundo. Era uma corrida de peças, com sorte e estratégia, popular em todas as classes sociais: há tabuleiros de Creta ao Sri Lanka, e alguém chegou a riscar um nas estátuas de touros alados com cabeça humana do palácio de Sargão II. Quando os tabuleiros foram redescobertos, ninguém sabia como jogar. No início dos anos 1980, o curador Irving Finkel traduziu uma tabuinha escrita pelo escriba Itti-Marduk-balāṭu, achada em 1880 nas ruínas da Babilônia, que descrevia as regras da época. Com ela e com o formato do tabuleiro, propôs como o jogo provavelmente funcionava. A tabuinha ainda trazia presságios para quem parasse em certas casas, como "você vai beber cerveja boa". O jogo sumiu do Oriente Médio na Antiguidade tardia, mas mercadores judeus aparentemente o levaram a Kochi. Lá ele continuou vivo, com vinte casas como o original, mas doze peças por jogador em vez de sete, até a comunidade começar a emigrar para Israel.

fontes.trecho: The Royal Game of Ur is a two-player strategy race board game of the tables family that was first played in ancient Mesopotamia during the early third millennium BC. The game was popular across the Middle East among people of all social strata, and boards for playing it have been found at locations as far away from Mesopotamia as Crete and Sri Lanka. One board, held by the British Museum, is dated to c. 2600 – c. 2400 BC, making it one of the oldest game boards in the world. [...] The Game of Ur remained popular until late antiquity, when it stopped being played, possibly either evolving into, or being displaced by, a form of tables game. It was eventually forgotten everywhere except among the Jewish population of the Indian city of Kochi, who continued playing a version of it called 'Asha' until the 1950s when they began emigrating to Israel. The Game of Ur received its name because it was first rediscovered by the English archaeologist Sir Leonard Woolley during his excavations of the Royal Cemetery at Ur between 1922 and 1934. [...] Like modern backgammon, the game combines elements of both strategy and luck. [...] A graffito version of the game carved with a sharp object, possibly a dagger, was discovered on one of the human-headed winged bull gate sentinels from the palace of Sargon II [...] such as "You will find a friend", "You will become powerful like a lion", or "You will draw fine beer". [...] At some point before the game fell out of popularity in the Middle East, it was apparently introduced to the Indian city of Kochi by a group of Jewish merchants. [...] The Kochi version of the game had twenty squares, just like the original Mesopotamian version, but each player had twelve pieces rather than seven, and the placement of the twenty squares was slightly different. [...] When the Game of Ur was first discovered, no one knew how it was played. Then, in the early 1980s, Irving Finkel, a curator at the British Museum, translated a clay tablet written c. 177 BC by the Babylonian scribe Itti-Marduk-balāṭu describing how the game was played during that time period [...] It had been discovered in 1880 in the ruins of Babylon and sold to the British Museum. [...] Based on these rules and the shape of the gameboard, Finkel was able to reconstruct how the game might have been played.

gancho: O senet, jogo egípcio de 30 casas, ganhou sentido religioso: no Livro dos Mortos, o falecido joga contra um adversário invisível. Na tumba de Tutancâmon havia tabuleiros com senet de um lado e o jogo de Ur do outro.
explicacao: O nome do jogo vem de uma palavra egípcia que quer dizer "passagem". A pintura mais antiga que o mostra com certeza está na tumba de Hesy-Re, de cerca de 2620 a.C., e há fragmentos que podem ser de senet em túmulos ainda mais antigos. O tabuleiro tinha 30 casas, em três fileiras de dez, e cada jogador movia cinco peões. Ao longo de uns 2.000 anos o equipamento quase não mudou, mas o significado sim: pelo menos a partir do Novo Império (1550 a 1077 a.C.), o percurso das peças representava a passagem do ka, a essência vital da alma, pelo duat, o mundo dos mortos. Um estudo sobre um tabuleiro dessa época mostrou o jogo deixando a origem secular para virar objeto religioso. Os egípcios também gostavam do jogo de Ur, e os quatro tabuleiros parecidos com ele achados na tumba de Tutancâmon vinham com caixinhas para dados e peças; muitos tinham um senet no verso, e bastava virar para trocar de jogo. O senet caiu em desuso no período romano, e as regras originais se perderam. As que vêm nos jogos vendidos hoje são reconstruções modernas, feitas por historiadores como Timothy Kendall e R. C. Bell.

fontes.trecho: lit. 'passing'; cf. Coptic ⲥⲓⲛⲉ /sinə/, 'passing, afternoon') is a board game from ancient Egypt that consists of ten or more pawns on a 30-square playing board. The earliest representation of senet is dated to c. 2620 BCE from the Mastaba of Hesy-Re [...] Even though the game has a 2,000-year history in Egypt, there appears to be very little variation in terms of key components. [...] However, the game fell out of use during the Roman period, and its original rules are the subject of conjecture. [...] Fragmentary boards that could be senet have been found in First Dynasty burials in Egypt, c. 3100 BCE. [...] Tutankhamun's tomb also contained the game. Senet is depicted in ancient texts, including in Chapter 17 of the Book of the Dead, where the individual who has died plays the game against an invisible opponent. [...] showed the evolution of the game from its secular origins into a more religious artefact. [...] the layout of the board was a grid of 30 squares, called "houses", arranged in three rows of ten. A complete senet game set would have contained a distinct set of five pawns for each of the two players. [...] At least by the New Kingdom in Egypt (1550–1077 BCE), the game reflected the concept of the ka (vital essence of the soul) passing through the duat (underworld) [...] historians Timothy Kendall and R. C. Bell have made their own reconstructions of the game rules. [...] However, their rules have been adopted by sellers of modern senet sets.

Four gameboards bearing a very close resemblance to the Royal Game of Ur were found in the tomb of Tutankhamun. These boards came with small boxes to store dice and game pieces and many had senet boards on the reverse sides so that the same board could be used to play either game and merely had to be flipped over.

gancho: O Monopoly, que no Brasil virou Banco Imobiliário, descende de um jogo criado por Elizabeth Magie para mostrar como os aluguéis enriquecem os donos de terra e empobrecem os inquilinos. Ela o patenteou em 1904.
explicacao: Magie desenhou o Landlord's Game entre 1902 e 1903 e o testou em Arden, no estado americano de Delaware. Ela seguia o georgismo, as ideias econômicas de Henry George, e queria uma "demonstração prática" do sistema de apropriação de terras e de suas consequências. Esperava também que as crianças, ao jogar, sentissem a injustiça e levassem essa percepção para a vida adulta. A caixa trazia dois conjuntos de regras: um premiava a formação de monopólios e a quebra dos rivais; no outro, "antimonopolista", o jogo terminava quando o jogador mais pobre dobrava o seu capital inicial. Versões caseiras se espalharam entre estudantes e professores de economia, e quacres de Atlantic City trocaram os nomes das propriedades por lugares da cidade. Em 1932, um casal ensinou essa versão a Charles Darrow, que passou a vendê-la como Monopoly e dizia tê-la inventado. A Parker Brothers comprou o jogo dele e, ao saber que ele não era o único criador, pagou 500 dólares por uma patente de Magie. Um erro de grafia do tabuleiro caseiro do casal, Marvin Gardens no lugar de Marven Gardens, passou para o jogo oficial. No Brasil, a Estrela lançou em 1944 a versão licenciada, o Banco Imobiliário.

fontes.trecho: The Landlord's Game is a board game patented in 1904 by Elizabeth Magie as U.S. patent 748,626. A realty and taxation game intended to educate users about Georgism, it is the inspiration for the 1935 board game Monopoly. [...] In 1902 to 1903, Magie designed the game and playtested it in Arden, Delaware. The game was created to be a "practical demonstration of the present system of land grabbing with all its usual outcomes and consequences". She based the game on the economic principles of Georgism, a system proposed by Henry George, with the object of demonstrating how rents enrich property owners and impoverish tenants. [...] Magie also hoped that when played by children the game would provoke their natural suspicion of unfairness, and that they might carry this awareness into adulthood. [...] Among the Atlantic City and Philadelphia communities of Quakers, the game was particularly popular with college students and economics professors. Jesse and Eugene Raiford, Quakers in Atlantic City, used household items instead of pawns and changed the properties' names to match well-known places in Atlantic City. [...] The set had rules for two different games, anti-monopolist and monopolist. The anti-monopolist rules reward all players during wealth creation, whereas the monopolist rules incentivize forming monopolies and forcing opponents out of the game. In the anti-monopolist or single-tax version (later called "Prosperity"), the game is won when the player with the least money doubles their original stake. [...] The company had recently started distributing Monopoly, which it had purchased from Charles Darrow who claimed to have invented it.

Charles Todd of Philadelphia recalled the day in 1932 when his childhood friend Esther Jones and her husband, Charles Darrow, came to his house for dinner. After the meal, the Todds introduced Darrow to The Landlord's Game, which they then played several times. [...] After that night, Darrow went on to utilize it to distribute the game himself as Monopoly. [...] The Parker Brothers bought the game's copyrights from Darrow. When the company learned Darrow was not the sole inventor of the game, it bought the rights to Magie's patent for $500. [...] Marvin Gardens, the furthest yellow property, is a misspelling of its actual name, Marven Gardens. The misspelling was introduced by Charles and Olive Todd, who taught the game to Charles Darrow. It was passed on when their homemade Monopoly board was copied by Darrow and then by Parker Brothers.

Banco Imobiliário é um jogo de tabuleiro lançado no Brasil pela Brinquedos Estrela. É uma variação local do jogo internacionalmente conhecido como Monopoly. [...] embora sua versão oficialmente licenciada pela Brinquedos Estrela só tenha sido lançada em 1944, sob o nome Banco Imobiliário

gancho: Na Segunda Guerra, o serviço secreto britânico mandou a prisioneiros dos nazistas jogos de Monopoly com mapas de fuga, bússolas e dinheiro de verdade escondidos, em nome de entidades beneficentes falsas.
explicacao: A Convenção de Genebra permitia que prisioneiros recebessem pacotes de familiares e de organizações de ajuda. O MI9, setor britânico dedicado a fugas, aproveitou a brecha, mas seu chefe proibiu o uso dos pacotes da Cruz Vermelha, por medo de represálias se algo fosse descoberto. Em vez disso, o MI9 criou organizações de fachada, com papel timbrado convincente e endereços inventados, muitas vezes de prédios destruídos por bombardeios. No começo, só mandava produtos comuns, sem nada escondido, e usava os recibos assinados que os campos devolviam para saber o que chegava. Até o jornal velho usado como enchimento combinava com a cidade do suposto doador. Levou uns três meses para o contrabando começar. A peça-chave foi a Waddingtons, de Leeds, que tinha a licença do Monopoly no Reino Unido e sabia imprimir em seda: foi uma das primeiras a fazer os mapas de seda do MI9 e fabricou tabuleiros com itens de fuga escondidos. Às vezes, cédulas reais iam misturadas ao dinheiro do jogo. O MI9 também procurou a gravadora EMI para esconder mapas laminados dentro de discos de gramofone.

fontes.trecho: During World War II, the British Secret Service contacted Waddingtons, as the company could also print on silk, to make Monopoly sets that included escape maps, money, a compass and file, all hidden in copies of the game sent by fake POW relief charities to prisoners of war. [...] the British Secret Intelligence Service had John Waddington Ltd., the licensed manufacturer of the game in the United Kingdom, create a special edition for World War II prisoners of war held by the Nazis. Hidden inside these games were maps, compasses, real money, and other objects useful for escaping.

The Geneva Convention allowed prisoners to receive parcels from families and relief organisations. Crockatt, the head of MI9, was very strict about not using Red Cross parcels for of fear of reprisal if the hidden items were discovered. [...] MI9 invented fictitious cover organisations through which packages could be delivered to the POW camps. Realistic letterheads for the stationery were developed and fictitious addresses, often at blitzed premises, were used. [...] The prison camps permitted the return of signed receipts for the parcels, facilitating MI9 to track which items were able to be delivered into the camp. At first only genuine, unmodified goods were sent, allowing MI9 to gauge the timing and successful receipt of parcels. Care was taken to match packing materials, such as old newspapers, with the alleged locations of the fictitious donor organisations. [...] It took about three months for the first successes to be scored, enabling the delivery of illicit contents to begin. One of the earliest companies to print silk maps for MI9 was John Waddington & Co. of Leeds. The company also held the licence in the UK of the U.S. board game Monopoly and therefore manufactured Monopoly boards with items hidden in them. Actual currency was sometimes hidden within the Monopoly money. MI9 approached EMI, a phonograph record company, to hide maps laminated in records.

gancho: Um jogo de guerra prussiano de 1824 já tinha o equivalente aos "pontos de vida" dos games: as tropas sofriam perdas parciais sem sair do mapa. Era o Kriegsspiel, e o rei mandou dar um a cada regimento.
explicacao: Os jogos de guerra anteriores derivavam do xadrez: as peças andavam numa grade e, atacadas, saíam do tabuleiro. O nobre prussiano George Leopold von Reisswitz quis algo mais realista. Primeiro esculpiu um campo de batalha em areia úmida; em 1812, deu ao rei Frederico Guilherme III um armário com terreno de azulejos de porcelana e blocos que se moviam livremente. O filho, Georg Heinrich von Reisswitz, oficial subalterno, levou a ideia adiante. No jogo dele, as tropas podiam perder parte dos homens e seguir lutando, com baixas decididas por dados, e o tabuleiro eram mapas topográficos precisos, na escala de 1:8.000. A grande novidade foi o juiz: os jogadores escreviam ordens, e ele movia os blocos como achava que as tropas cumpririam. Só punha no mapa o que cada lado podia ver, simulando a névoa da guerra. Em 1824, o chefe do Estado-Maior declarou que aquilo não era um jogo comum, mas uma escola para a guerra, e o rei mandou entregar um conjunto a cada regimento. Foi o primeiro jogo de guerra adotado em larga escala por um exército. Depois da vitória prussiana sobre a França, na guerra de 1870, outros países criaram jogos parecidos.

fontes.trecho: Kriegsspiel is a genre of wargaming developed by the Prussian Army in the 19th century to teach battlefield tactics to officers. [...] After Prussia's impressive victory over France in the Franco-Prussian War, other countries began designing similar wargames for their own armies. [...] They were derivatives of chess, but the pieces represented real military units [...] a Prussian nobleman and wargaming enthusiast named George Leopold von Reisswitz set out to develop a more realistic wargame wherein the units could move about in a free-form manner over more natural terrain. Reisswitz first experimented with a table covered in a layer of damp sand. [...] In 1812, Reisswitz presented to the king a wooden table-cabinet. [...] Instead of sculpted sand, the battlefield was made out of porcelain tiles [...] Georg Heinrich Rudolf Johann von Reisswitz was a junior officer in the Prussian army. [...] In the earlier wargames of Hellwig and Venturini, units were like chess pieces in that when attacked, they were simply killed and removed from play, even if the pieces represented groups of soldiers. By contrast, units in Reisswitz's game could suffer partial losses yet still remain on the battlefield. [...] Reisswitz's game was thus the first to incorporate unit hitpoints. It also modeled variable damage: The casualties inflicted by an attacker on his enemy were determined using dice. Reisswitz Jr.'s game was designed to be played on accurate, large-scale (1:8,000) topographical maps. [...] Reisswitz Jr.'s great innovation, however, was the introduction of an umpire. The players did not directly control the troop blocks on the game map. Rather, they wrote down their orders for their troops and gave them to the umpire. [...] The game could simulate the fog of war, where the umpire would place on the map blocks only for the troops which were in visual range of both sides. [...] In early 1824, the prince invited Reisswitz Jr. to present his wargame to the king and his senior generals at Berlin Castle. [...] The Chief of the General Staff, General von Müffling declared: "this is no ordinary sort of game, this is schooling for war. [...] The king ordered that every regiment receive a Kriegsspiel set. [...] This was thus the first wargame to be widely adopted by a military as a serious tool for training and research. [...] The Austro-Prussian War of 1866 and the Franco-Prussian War of 1870 broke a long period of peace for the German states

gancho: A dama, peça mais forte do xadrez, por séculos só andava uma casa na diagonal: era o vizir, um conselheiro do rei. O movimento atual nasceu na Espanha do século XV, numa versão apelidada com desdém de "xadrez da louca".
explicacao: No xatranje, o jogo persa de onde veio essa peça, ela era o conselheiro, ou vizir: farzīn em persa, firz ou wazīr em árabe. Ela só se movia uma casa na diagonal. Por volta de 1300, ganhou o direito de saltar duas casas na primeira jogada. Na Europa, o nome foi ganhando forma feminina, e a peça virou rainha. No século XV, na Espanha, passou a somar os movimentos da torre e do bispo. Um poema valenciano já mostrava a regra nova, e o tratado mais antigo que sobreviveu a descrevê-la, de Luis Ramírez de Lucena, saiu durante o reinado de Isabel I de Castela. A historiadora Marilyn Yalom sugere que o poder da rainha Isabel pode ter inspirado a mudança. O "xadrez da dama", chamado pejorativamente na Itália de "xadrez da louca", espalhou-se rápido, ajudado pela imprensa. As regras novas enfrentaram resistência. E, em várias épocas, chegou-se a restringir a promoção de um peão a dama enquanto a original estivesse no tabuleiro, para não dar ao rei mais de uma rainha. Os nomes também dividiram a Europa: países católicos adotaram termos ligados a "senhora", como "dama", enquanto alemães e ingleses preferiram "rainha". Em russo, a peça ainda se chama ferz.

fontes.trecho: The predecessor to the queen is the ferz, a weak piece originating from the Persian game of shatranj, able to move or capture only one step diagonally. The queen acquired its modern move in Spain in the 15th century. [...] The queen was originally the counsellor or prime minister or vizier (Sanskrit mantri, Persian farzīn, Arabic firzān, firz or wazīr). Initially, its only move was one square diagonally. Around 1300, its abilities were enhanced to allow it to jump two squares diagonally (onto a same-colored square) for its first move. The fers changed into the queen over time. [...] The word fers became grammatically feminized in several languages [...] During the great chess reform at the end of the 15th century, Catholic nations kept using an equivalent of Latin domina ('lady'), such as dama in Spanish, donna in Italy, and dame in France [...] Protestant nations such as Germany and England, however, refused any derivatives of domina as it might have suggested some cult of the Virgin Mary, and instead opted for secular terms such as Königin in German and "queen" in English. In Russian, the piece keeps its Persian name of ferz [...] the earliest surviving treatise to describe the modern movement of the queen (as well as the bishop and pawn), Repetición de amores e arte de axedres con CL iuegos de partido ('Discourses on Love and the Art of Chess with 150 Problems') by Luis Ramírez de Lucena, was published during the reign of Isabella I of Castile. Even before that, the Valencian poem Scachs d'amor ("Chess of Love") depicted a chess game [...] The modern move of the queen started in Spain during Isabella I's reign, perhaps inspired by her great political power [...] During the 15th century, the queen's move took its modern form as a combination of the move of the rook and the current move of the bishop. Starting from Spain, this new version – called 'queen's chess' (in Italian, scacchi della donna) or, pejoratively, 'madwoman's chess' (scacchi alla rabiosa) – spread throughout Europe rapidly, partly due to the advent of the printing press and the popularity of new books on chess. The new rules faced a backlash in some quarters [...] At various times, the ability of pawns to be queened was restricted while the original queen was still on the board, so as not to cause scandal by providing the king with more than one queen.

gancho: Num tabuleiro de go de 2×2, com só quatro pontos, cabem 386.356.909.593 partidas diferentes. No tabuleiro oficial, de 19×19, as posições legais só foram contadas até o último algarismo em 2016: cerca de 2 × 10^170.
explicacao: Cada um dos 361 pontos do tabuleiro de go pode estar vazio, com pedra preta ou com pedra branca, o que dá 3^361 arranjos. Só parte deles é legal: todo grupo de pedras ligadas da mesma cor precisa tocar ao menos um ponto vazio, porque um grupo sem nenhum é capturado. Por causa dessa regra, as posições que podem surgir numa partida são exatamente as legais. Uma amostragem ao acaso, feita em 1992, já indicava que só cerca de 1,2% dos arranjos são legais, e o valor aproximado era conhecido desde 2006. Faltava o número exato. John Tromp e colegas reduziram a conta a elevar à 361ª potência uma matriz esparsa com 363 bilhões de linhas e colunas, e dividiram o trabalho em 9 partes independentes com o teorema chinês do resto. O cálculo rodou em servidores desde março de 2015, e o resultado saiu em 20 de janeiro de 2016. Para comparação, estima-se que o universo observável tenha cerca de 10^80 átomos. O número de partidas possíveis no tabuleiro grande é ainda mais absurdo: provou-se que passa de um googolplex.

fontes.titulo: Number of legal Go positions (John Tromp)
fontes.trecho: The 361 points on a 19x19 Go board can be colored empty, black, or white. Only some of the 3^361 possible positions are legal, namely those where every group of connected stones of the same color has an empty point adjacent to it. [...] Due to its capture rule, the positions that can arise in a game of Go are exactly the legal positions. On Jan 20, 2016, the number of legal positions on a standard size Go board was determined to be L19 = [...] This 1.2% chance was already computed by random sampling back in 1992. The approximation L19 ~ 2.081681994 * 10^170 has been known since 2006. [...] It essentially reduces computing L19 to taking the 361st power of a very sparse matrix of 363 billion rows and columns. [...] Clever use of the Chinese Remainder Theorem allows for splitting the computation into 9 independent parts [...] Starting from March 6 2015, running on big servers at the IAS [...] Few people believe that a tiny 2x2 Go board allows for more than a few hundred games. Yet 2x2 games number not in the hundreds, nor in the thousands, nor even in the millions. They number in the hundreds of billions! 386356909593 to be precise. [...] A lower bound of 10^{10^48} on the number of 19x19 games, as proved in our paper, was recently improved to a googolplex.

Tromp and Farnebäck derived a recursive formula for legal positions L(m,n) of a rectangle board with length m and n. The exact number of L(19,19) was obtained in 2016. [...] It has been estimated that the observable universe contains around 1080 atoms, far fewer than the number of possible legal positions of regular board size (m=n=19).

gancho: Em 2007, provou-se que nas damas de regra inglesa (checkers), com jogo perfeito dos dois lados, a partida sempre empata. Tido como o maior de todos, Marion Tinsley perdeu só sete partidas de 1950 até morrer, em 1995.
explicacao: Tinsley era matemático, com doutorado em análise combinatória, e foi campeão mundial de 1955 a 1958 e de 1975 a 1991, sem nunca perder um match pelo título. Das sete derrotas em mais de quatro décadas, duas foram para o Chinook, programa da Universidade de Alberta criado por uma equipe liderada por Jonathan Schaeffer. Tudo o que o Chinook sabia foi programado pelos autores, sem aprendizado de máquina, e ele tinha um banco de dados com todas as posições de oito peças ou menos. Em 1990, ficou em segundo, atrás de Tinsley, no campeonato dos EUA, o que daria direito a disputar o título mundial. As federações recusaram um computador, e Tinsley renunciou ao título para poder enfrentá-lo. Em 1992, venceu por 4 a 2, com 33 empates. Na revanche, em 1994, abandonou depois de seis empates, por problemas de saúde; tinha um câncer no pâncreas e morreu meses depois. O Chinook virou o primeiro programa campeão mundial contra humanos, mas nunca venceu Tinsley num match. Em 1995, depois de defender o título contra outro humano, Schaeffer tirou o Chinook das competições e foi tentar resolver o jogo. Em julho de 2007, a revista Science publicou a prova: o melhor que alguém consegue contra um adversário perfeito é o empate.

fontes.trecho: Marion Franklin Tinsley (February 3, 1927 – April 3, 1995) was an American mathematician and checkers player. He is widely considered the greatest checkers player ever. Tinsley was world champion from 1955–1958 and 1975–1991 and never lost a world championship match. He lost only seven games (two to the Chinook computer program, one in a simultaneous exhibition) from 1950 until his death in 1995. [...] Tinsley had a doctorate from Ohio State University in the mathematical discipline of combinatorial analysis. [...] In August 1992, he defeated the Chinook computer program 4–2 (with 33 draws) in a match. [...] Unable to appeal their decision, Tinsley resigned his title as World Champion and immediately indicated his desire to play against Chinook. [...] In August 1994, a second match with Chinook was organized, but Tinsley withdrew after only six games (all draws) for health reasons. [...] Tinsley was diagnosed with pancreatic cancer a week after the match, and died seven months later.

Chinook is a computer program that plays checkers (also known as draughts). It was developed between the years 1989 to 2007 at the University of Alberta, by a team led by Jonathan Schaeffer [...] an end-game database for all positions with eight pieces or fewer. All of Chinook's knowledge was programmed by its creators, rather than learned using an artificial intelligence system. [...] In 1990 Chinook won the right to play in the human World Championship by being second to Marion Tinsley in the US Nationals. At first, the American Checkers Federation and English Draughts Association were against the participation of a computer in a human championship. [...] This made Chinook the first computer program to win a world championship title in a competition against humans, but while Chinook became the world champion, it never defeated Tinsley, who was significantly superior to even his closest peers. [...] After the match, Jonathan Schaeffer decided not to let Chinook compete any more, but instead try to solve checkers. [...] July 19, 2007 - The journal Science publishes Schaeffer's team's article "Checkers Is Solved", presenting their proof that the best a player can achieve playing against a player with perfect information is a draw. [...] In 1995, Chinook defended its man-machine title against Don Lafferty in a 32-game match.

gancho: O jogo de cobras e escadas vem de um jogo indiano de lição moral: escadas eram virtudes; cobras, vícios. Havia mais cobras que escadas, pois o caminho do bem é mais difícil. A versão inglesa igualou o número.
explicacao: Na Índia, o jogo era conhecido como Moksha Patam, a "lição da libertação", e fazia parte de uma família de jogos indianos de dados que inclui o pachisi, do qual descendem o Ludo e outros jogos de percurso. As escadas representavam virtudes como generosidade, fé e humildade; as cobras, vícios como luxúria, raiva, assassinato e roubo. A mensagem: fazendo o bem, a pessoa alcança a libertação espiritual, o moksha; fazendo o mal, renasce em formas de vida inferiores. A versão ligada ao jainismo se chamava gyan chauper, o "jogo da sabedoria", e havia uma de inspiração sufi no mundo muçulmano. A versão inglesa mais antiga conhecida foi registrada em 1892. Na Inglaterra vitoriana, os valores indianos deram lugar a outros: escadas de Economia, Penitência e Trabalho levavam à Graça e ao Sucesso, e cobras de Indulgência, Desobediência e Preguiça levavam à Doença, à Desgraça e à Pobreza. Nos EUA, a Milton Bradley lança desde 1943 uma versão de tom também moralista, Chutes and Ladders. Em Tamil Nadu, devotos de Vishnu jogam a versão local para ficar acordados numa noite de festival.

fontes.trecho: The game originated in ancient India as Moksha Patam ('liberation lesson'), and was brought to the United Kingdom in the 1890s. [...] The historic version had its roots in morality lessons, on which a player's progression up the board represented a life journey complicated by virtues (ladders) and vices (snakes). The game is also sold under other names, such as the morality themed Chutes and Ladders published by the Milton Bradley Company starting in 1943. [...] Snakes and ladders originated as part of a family of Indian dice board games. They included gyan chauper and pachisi (which was adapted into Ludo, Parcheesi, and other cross and circle games). [...] The ladders represented virtues such as generosity, faith, and humility, while the snakes represented vices such as lust, anger, murder, and theft. The morality lesson of the game was that a person can attain liberation (Moksha) through doing good, whereas by doing evil one will be reborn as lower forms of life. The number of ladders was fewer than the number of snakes as a reminder that a path of good is much more difficult to tread than a path of sins. [...] Gyan chauper, or jnan chauper, (game of wisdom), the version associated with the Jain philosophy, encompassed the concepts like karma and Moksha. A version popular in the Muslim world is known as shatranj al-'urafa and exists in various versions in India, Iran, and Turkey. In this version, based on sufi philosophy [...] The earliest known English version of Snakes and Ladders was by F. H. Ayres, registered in October 1892. [...] In Victorian England, the Indian virtues and vices were replaced by English ones in hopes of better reflecting Victorian doctrines of morality. Squares of Fulfilment, Grace, and Success were accessible by ladders of Thrift, Penitence, and Industry, and snakes of Indulgence, Disobedience, and Indolence caused one to end up in Illness, Disgrace, and Poverty.
